headings.text: 10 Non-Carbonated Drinks for a Healthier You: Hydration and Beyond
Hydrating non-carbonated drinks to benefit your health

structured_data.articleBody:
When it comes to your overall health, hydration is vital. What you may not realize is that the type of fluids that you put into your body are just as important as making sure you're getting enough liquids each day. We understand that plain old water can get boring, but sugary sodas and fruit juices aren't the only options out there. 
If you're thinking of sparkling waters and carbonated energy drinks, those are great alternatives, but they're best enjoyed in moderation. Too much carbonation can lead to bloating and gas. At the same time, the citric acid that gives these drinks their bite can actually erode the enamel on your teeth. 
For today's healthful drinks, we're going to focus on non-carbonated beverages that are still hydrating and good for you.
Hydrating non-carbonated drinks to benefit your health
Coconut water
As a natural source of electrolytes, coconut water is one of the most hydrating drinks around. It's a great source of potassium, magnesium, and calcium while being low in calories and in sugar. 
Coconut water is also a source of antioxidants which are beneficial for your overall health. Its natural sweetness and electrolytes make it the perfect source of hydration post-workout or on a hot summer day. 

You can pick up some coconut water at your local health food store or supermarket. If you're feeling adventurous, don't be shy to try it straight from a coconut should you get the opportunity!
Herbal tea
There are endless varieties of herbal tea available, many of which boast some great health benefits. These caffeine-free varieties can be enjoyed hot or cold and are a flavorful alternative to sugary juices and sodas.
Some popular herbal teas that offer health benefits include ginseng tea for a great immune system boost, ginger tea to help with digestion, chamomile for relaxation, and hibiscus for its antioxidant-rich polyphenols that have been linked with improved heart health. 
All of these are calorie and sugar-free. Try out a few different kinds to see which ones you like best!
Hot water with lemon
This is a simple but effective drink that offers some great health benefits in addition to getting you hydrated first thing in the morning. Hot water with lemon is a great way to start your day as the hot water aids in digestion while the lemon provides Vitamin C and antioxidants that help to reduce inflammation.  
If you're feeling under the weather, this drink is also great for helping to boost your immune system. Additionally, the vitamin C can help relieve a sore throat and help you fight infection.
Vegetable juice
Like fruit juices, vegetable juices are a great way to get in your daily recommended servings of vegetables. However, they don't contain the same amount of sugar as their fruity counterparts. 
In addition to being hydrating, vegetable juice is packed with vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants that are essential for good health. Some popular vegetable juices include beet juice for its high levels of nitrates, which can improve blood flow and lower blood pressure; carrot juice for its beta-carotene content that is beneficial for eye health; and cucumber juice for its anti-inflammatory properties. 
You can make these yourself if you've got a juicer at home or try a few varieties from your local smoothie shop or health food store.
Green tea
Green tea is an excellent non-carbonated drink choice that offers a number of health benefits. In addition to being hydrating, green tea is loaded with antioxidants that can help improve your overall health. 
Some of the key antioxidants found in green tea include catechins and polyphenols, which have been linked with decreased cancer risk, improved heart health, and reduced inflammation. Green tea is also a great source of caffeine if you're looking for a bit of a pick-me-up without the sugar crash that comes with energy drinks. 

Since green tea does contain caffeine, it's still best to limit yourself to 1-2 cups a day. This way, you can enjoy the hydration and health benefits without aggravating your stomach with the diuretic properties.
Watermelon juice
Watermelon juice is a great hydrating drink choice that is also packed with nutrients. Like the fruit itself, watermelon juice is high in lycopene, an antioxidant linked with decreased cancer risk and improved heart health.
Not only is it a tasty source of hydration, but watermelon juice also contains potassium which can help to regulate blood pressure. Just make sure to read the ingredients for any added sugar if you're not making yours at home.
Pomegranate juice
Pomegranate juice is another excellent choice for a hydrating and healthy drink. This juice is higher in antioxidants than most other fruit juices, including polyphenols and anthocyanins, which have been linked with improved reduced inflammation and heart health. 
It can be an acquired taste as it is quite tart, but many people enjoy it for its health benefits. Like watermelon juice, be sure to watch out for added sugar in store-bought versions.
Kombucha
Kombucha is a fermented tea that's full of probiotics, making it great for gut health. It's also a great source of antioxidants and anti-inflammatories. While it is carbonated, it is actually naturally occurring through the fermentation process. However, you can allow it to flatten if you prefer non-carbonated drinks. 

Is flat kombucha still good for you? The answer is a resounding yes! Flat kombucha still has all of the same nutritional components and health benefits as the bubbly kind. There are a number of different kombucha brands on the market today so look for those with little to no added sugars to get the most out of this healthy drink.
Fruit-infused waters
Fruit-infused waters are a great way to add flavor to your water without adding any calories or sugar. You can make these yourself by adding fresh fruits to a pitcher of water and letting them sit overnight in the fridge. 
The hint of flavor helps to make water more appealing while imparting some added nutrients and antioxidants. Some great combinations to try include raspberry and lime, strawberry and basil, or even cucumber and mint.
Halfday Iced Tea
If you're looking for a non-carbonated drink with a bit of caffeine, Halfday tea tonics are a great choice. Compared to the classic canned and bottled iced teas on the market, Halfday isn't filled with preservatives, sugar, or any artificial flavors. Our iced teas are only 35-40 calories with 3-4g of natural sugar. 

Not only do these iced teas taste great, but they're also great for your gut. Each can contains 8g of fiber and a healthy dose of prebiotics to keep the good bacteria in your gut happy and healthy. Now that you know that flat kombucha is still good for you, you can feed those probiotics with the prebiotics found in every can of Halfday, creating a healthy gut microbiome.
Hydrate yourself with any one of our delicious flavors, or get them all in our variety 12-pack.  
 

 
There are plenty of great non-carbonated drinks out there that can help improve your overall health. Whether you're looking for something hydrating, antioxidant-rich, or gut-friendly, there's definitely a drink to fit the bill.  
Hydrating yourself shouldn't have to be boring, but it doesn't need to be unhealthy either. So, next time you're looking for a refreshing drink to quench your thirst, ditch the sodas and sparkling waters, switch to one of these healthy non-carbonated alternatives instead. Your body will thank you!

You can make these yourself if you've got a juicer at home or try a few varieties from your local smoothie shop or health food store. Green tea Green tea is an excellent non-carbonated drink choice that offers a number of health benefits. In addition to being hydrating, green tea is loaded with antioxidants that can help improve your overall health. Some of the key antioxidants found in green tea include catechins and polyphenols, which have been linked with decreased cancer risk, improved heart health, and reduced inflammation. Green tea is also a great source of caffeine if you're looking for a bit of a pick-me-up without the sugar crash that comes with energy drinks. Since green tea does contain caffeine, it's still best to limit yourself to 1-2 cups a day. This way, you can enjoy the hydration and health benefits without aggravating your stomach with the diuretic properties. Watermelon juice Watermelon juice is a great hydrating drink choice that is also packed with nutrients. Like the fruit itself, watermelon juice is high in lycopene, an antioxidant linked with decreased cancer risk and improved heart health. Not only is it a tasty source of hydration, but watermelon juice also contains potassium which can help to regulate blood pressure. Just make sure to read the ingredients for any added sugar if you're not making yours at home. Pomegranate juice Pomegranate juice is another excellent choice for a hydrating and healthy drink. This juice is higher in antioxidants than most other fruit juices, including polyphenols and anthocyanins, which have been linked with improved reduced inflammation and heart health. It can be an acquired taste as it is quite tart, but many people enjoy it for its health benefits. Like watermelon juice, be sure to watch out for added sugar in store-bought versions. Kombucha Kombucha is a fermented tea that's full of probiotics , making it great for gut health. It's also a great source of antioxidants and anti-inflammatories. While it is carbonated, it is actually naturally occurring through the fermentation process. However, you can allow it to flatten if you prefer non-carbonated drinks. Is flat kombucha still good for you? The answer is a resounding yes! Flat kombucha still has all of the same nutritional components and health benefits as the bubbly kind. There are a number of different kombucha brands on the market today so look for those with little to no added sugars to get the most out of this healthy drink. Fruit-infused waters Fruit-infused waters are a great way to add flavor to your water without adding any calories or sugar. You can make these yourself by adding fresh fruits to a pitcher of water and letting them sit overnight in the fridge. The hint of flavor helps to make water more appealing while imparting some added nutrients and antioxidants. Some great combinations to try include raspberry and lime, strawberry and basil, or even cucumber and mint. Halfday Iced Tea If you're looking for a non-carbonated drink with a bit of caffeine, Halfday tea tonics are a great choice. Compared to the classic canned and bottled iced teas on the market, Halfday isn't filled with preservatives, sugar, or any artificial flavors. Our iced teas are only 35-40 calories with 3-4g of natural sugar. Not only do these iced teas taste great, but they're also great for your gut. Each can contains 8g of fiber and a healthy dose of prebiotics to keep the good bacteria in your gut happy and healthy. Now that you know that flat kombucha is still good for you, you can feed those probiotics with the prebiotics found in every can of Halfday, creating a healthy gut microbiome. Hydrate yourself with any one of our delicious flavors, or get them all in our variety 12-pack . There are plenty of great non-carbonated drinks out there that can help improve your overall health. Whether you're looking for something hydrating, antioxidant-rich, or gut-friendly, there's definitely a drink to fit the bill. Hydrating yourself shouldn't have to be boring, but it doesn't need to be unhealthy either. So, next time you're looking for a refreshing drink to quench your thirst, ditch the sodas and sparkling waters, switch to one of these healthy non-carbonated alternatives instead. Your body will thank you! Back to blog

headings.text: 4 Healthy Iced Tea Recipes for a Refreshing Summer Drink
How to brew iced tea at home
Our favorite healthy iced tea recipes
Bonus: Have a Halfday tea tonic!

structured_data.articleBody:
Summertime is the perfect time to enjoy a delicious and refreshing glass of iced tea. But if you've ever checked the nutrition facts of those popular supermarket brands, you know that they're often loaded with sugar, preservatives, and unhealthy additives.
If you're looking for healthy options, why not make your own iced tea at home? Luckily, it's easy to make with just a few simple ingredients. In this blog post, we will discuss the 3 ways to brew iced tea at home and share 4 of our favorite healthy iced tea recipes. 

Whether you prefer an earthy iced green tea or something on the fruitier side, we have something for everyone! So relax, and enjoy a cold glass of healthy iced tea this summer.
How to brew iced tea at home
There are three main methods for brewing iced tea: hot brew, ice chill, and cold brew. 
Hot Brew: This is the most common method for making iced tea. To hot brew, simply make a pot of tea using your favorite loose leaf tea or tea bags. Once brewed, allow it to cool for up to 2 hours and enjoy it over ice. 
Ice Chill: This method is ideal for those who are looking for the quickest way to enjoy their iced tea. However, you're going to need a lot of ice. Brew your hot tea as you usually would then pour it into a large bowl or pitcher filled to the top with ice. Stir until the tea is chilled, and then drink immediately. Note: this may dilute the tea slightly so you can brew your tea a little stronger. 
Cold Brew:  This method may take the longest, but it produces the absolute best-iced tea that is free of any bitterness or cloudiness. Just like cold brew coffee, cold brew tea uses time instead of heat to extract all the flavors from your tea leaves. 
To cold brew, add loose leaf tea or tea bags to a large pitcher or jar and then fill it with cold water. Allow your tea to steep for at least 6 hours, preferably 12 hours if you've got the time. Stir occasionally and then strain out the tea leaves once complete. Serve over ice, and enjoy!
Homebrewing tips:

Use filtered water to make the tastiest tea.
Brew your iced tea stronger than you would typically drink it to avoid dilution from the ice.
If you need to add sweetness, liquid sugar will incorporate best. Combine equal parts water and sugar and stir until the water dissolves, creating a simple syrup. We recommend liquid Stevia for a healthier alternative.
Your home-brewed iced tea will last in the fridge for 4-5 days.

Our favorite healthy iced tea recipes
Now that you know how to brew iced tea at home, it's time to try some of our favorite healthy recipes!
Iced Green Tea with Mint:
This iced green tea is perfect for those looking for a refreshing and healthy drink. The addition of mint gives it a light, refreshing flavor perfect for summer. 

Each recipe below will follow the ice chill or hot brew method for the sake of timing, but you can cold brew these recipes using the same measurements. 
Ingredients:


 Mint leaves


 4 green tea bags


 1 lemon


 Honey or your preferred sweetener (optional)


Directions:

Boil 4 cups of filtered water in a saucepan, then remove from the heat. Add 2 sprigs of mint along with 4 green tea bags and allow to steep for 10 minutes.
Discard the tea bags and mint. Add in 2 tbsp of honey and stir until dissolved. Add more to taste.
Pour your green tea mixture into a large pitcher with 2 cups of cold water, 2 cups of ice, and additional sprigs of mint.
Once cooled, serve your iced green tea with a mint sprig and a lemon slice and enjoy.

Lychee Thai Iced Tea
This lychee Thai iced tea recipe is perfect for those who are looking for a unique and flavorful iced tea. The lychees add a lovely sweetness, while the black tea provides a rich, earthy flavor. 
Ingredients: 


 6 bags of Thai black tea (black tea will also work)


 1 can of lychees in syrup


 1 lemon 

Directions: 

Strain your lychees to separate the fruit from the syrup. Freeze your lychees and chill your syrup in the refrigerator. *You can either use the syrup as your primary sweetener or use a sugar-free lychee syrup instead.
Steep your 6 tea bags in a pot of boiling water until the liquid becomes a deep orange.
Pour into a pitcher to chill in the refrigerator.
Once chilled, add your frozen lychee and ice cubes to the pitcher of tea. Add lychee syrup to taste until it reaches your desired sweetness.
Garnish with a slice of lemon, serve over ice, and enjoy your very own lychee Thai iced tea.

Iced Matcha Lemonade
This healthy iced matcha lemonade is perfect for a hot summer day. The combination of matcha and lemon is light, refreshing, and oh so delicious. 
Ingredients:


 Juice of 1 lemon


 1 cup of cold water


 Liquid sweetener of choice (equivalent to 1 tbsp of simple syrup)


 1 teaspoon matcha powder 

Directions:

Make your lemonade. In a shaker, combine a 1/2 cup of water, the juice of your lemon, and 1 tbsp of your sweetener. Give it about 10-15 shakes until combined.
Pour your lemonade into a glass.
Rinse your shaker. Add a 1/2 cup of water into your shaker with a teaspoon of matcha powder. Shake until combined, about 10-15 shakes.
Pour your matcha over your lemonade with your desired amount of ice. Stir, sip, and enjoy!

Fruity Hibiscus Iced Tea
This fruity iced hibiscus tea is perfect for those who are looking for a healthy and delicious summer drink full of antioxidants. Hibiscus tea is known for its various health benefits, including lowering blood pressure and reducing blood sugar levels. This tea has a beautiful red color, and the tart flavor is balanced by the sweetness of the added fruits.  

Ingredients:


 4 bags of hibiscus tea


 1 quart of water


 Sweetener of your choice


 1 sliced orange


 1 sliced lime


 1 sliced lemon


 1 cup of sliced strawberries


 Several sprigs of fresh mint 

Directions : 

Allow your hibiscus tea bags to steep in the quart of boiled water until it reaches a deep red color.
Pour into a heat-proof pitcher and add all of your sliced fruit.
Once the mixture reaches room temperature, add your mint.
Chill your tea mixture in the refrigerator.
Once chilled, sweeten to taste. Try a sugar-free mint sweetener if you prefer a more intense mint flavor.
Pour into a tall glass and enjoy!

Bonus: Have a Halfday tea tonic!
Homemade healthy iced teas are fantastic, but sometimes you really just want the convenience of a canned iced tea. That's where Halfday comes in. Our healthy iced teas are made with real organic ingredients and are sweetened with stevia, so they taste great without all the sugar.

 
Halfday lets you enjoy all the classic iced tea favorites from your childhood but without any of the unhealthy junk. Instead, you'll be getting 8g of fiber and healthy prebiotics in every can. 
There you have it, 5 healthy iced tea options perfect for summer. Whether you're looking for a refreshing iced green tea, a unique Thai iced tea, or an antioxidant-rich hibiscus tea, there's something here for everyone. And don't forget about Halfday teas--our healthy canned iced teas are perfect for when you're on the go.
So what are you waiting for? Grab a healthy iced tea and enjoy the summer!

8 Best Fiber Cereals To Keep You Healthy
 – Halfday Iced Tea
pages.description: Increasing fiber intake in your diet is easy with fiber-rich breakfast cereals. Listed below are the 8 best fiber cereals!

headings.text: 8 Best Fiber Cereals To Keep You Healthy
Drinking Tea with Your Morning Cereal

structured_data.articleBody:
Fiber intake is an essential part of our diet. Fiber is necessary regardless of a person's shape or size because of the function that it has in our body. It is well-known for making our gut healthier and improving digestion. If a person is dealing with constipation, the doctor will likely prescribe medicine that contains fiber or foods that are quite high in fiber. Not only that, fiber tends to speed up our metabolism because it speeds up digestion. However, the worst part is that fiber is found in very little quantity in most diets.
People don't avoid the intake of fiber consciously. It is just not found in ample quantities in the food that we eat every day.



It has been discovered that eating a certain amount of fiber in the morning will not only improve digestive health but will help clear our stomach of any waste substances from the previous day. This, in turn, will reduce bloating and allow you to feel much fitter. Eating fiber in the morning is possible if you eat an appropriate quantity of food and the correct type of food. It has also been made easier for people because of the wide range of breakfast cereals available in the market.
8 Best Fiber Cereals
1.    Fiber One

Fiber One is a fiber-rich breakfast cereal that you will find on many lists concerning healthy cereals. Perhaps, one of the selling points of this cereal is that it has zero added sugar. This will protect your body from any unnecessary fats added for the sake of flavor. Each serving of this cereal contains about 18g of fiber which is a decent amount of fiber for any food. For comparison, this amount of fiber is found in at least 2 servings of fruit, making it one of the best fiber cereals.
2.    Wheat n' Bran

Wheat n' Bran is another excellent cereal that is on this list. The zero-sugar aspect of this cereal allows people to enjoy it without worrying about putting on the pounds. Wheat n' Bran gives the consumer at least 9g of fiber with almost every serving. Shredded wheat is perfect for digestion because of the expanded surface area that is easier to break down. Shredded wheat is also perfect for people looking to lose weight and get rid of bloating. This cereal is the ideal cereal for a weight-conscious person who wants to improve their figure.
3.    Grape Nuts

Another decent cereal that is available in the market is grape nuts. As evident by the title, the exquisite combination of grapes and nuts in your morning cereal is the perfect way to start the day. Not everyone is a fan of dry cereals, even if the cereal is high in fiber. The fruits and the nuts keep things interesting while also providing your body with the fiber it needs. It's important to keep things in control while also satisfying your taste buds, and this cereal does the trick making it one of the best fiber cereals in the market.
4.    Fiber One Honey Clusters

It is a popular belief that honey is the ideal alternative for sugar, and it is true. Honey consumed in large amounts may be bad for you in the long run, but the amount present in the Honey Clusters is the perfect ratio of sweetness that you need. Honey Clusters are granola-based, giving the extra cereal crunch that one needs for mouth satisfaction. The cereal may not have zero sugar, but it is quite low at 6 grams of sugar which is almost negligible considering the amount of fiber that one is getting; hence, it is among the best fiber cereals.
5.    Alpen Muesli

Muesli is quite a delicacy in many regions of the world, and America is no different. Muesli can make any breakfast more delicious and give your mouth a nice texture to chew on. Alpen Muesli is no different. It is high in fiber content; every serving has at least 7g of fiber going into your body. It also contains a hefty 8g of protein. The fiber is a healthy combination of soluble and insoluble fiber that is good for you.
6.    Kellogg's All-Bran

The term "all-bran" written on any cereal box should be your go-to sign that the cereal is rich in fiber. When the gluten content in any type of food is whole and not polished and preserved, the food is likely to have a high fiber content. If you choose this cereal, you will be receiving around 12g of fiber with every serving that you put in your body. Not only that, but this cereal is also an excellent source of vitamin D. If you have blood-pressure issues, this cereal may be perfect for you because of the low sodium content in it.
7.    Nature's Path Smart Bran

Another good whole cereal on this list is the Nature's Path Smart Bran cereal. Bran is a type of wheat that is left whole. It gives you that crude taste in your mouth which ensures you that you are eating healthy. All the while, you will not have to compromise on your taste buds because the cereal tastes delicious with a bit of splash of milk. In addition to that, the cereal also contains psyllium husk. Psyllium husk is a substance known to lower cholesterol in the body.
8.    Kashi Go Cereal

Kashi Go cereals are not only high in fiber but are also high in protein. Much like fiber, the everyday man has trouble getting enough protein in their body. This is because of the increased amount of processed food in the market.
Maybe one of the off-putting elements of these cereals is that they contain sugar. However, the sugar content isn't that high, and a little sugar never killed anyone. If you are not obese or overweight, this sugar is perfectly fine for your body especially considering that they give a high amount of fiber to the body.
Drinking Tea with Your Morning Cereal
It should come as no surprise that for a healthy breakfast, the fluids that you consume with the breakfast do matter. Many people will often opt for a sugary coffee filled to the brim with syrups and creamers that aren't always good for you, especially if you consume them regularly. The perfect alternative would be to opt for a cup of tea. Tea is a better source of caffeine in the morning. It is not overpowering and does not contain many calories from sugar and carbs. The HalfDay Tea comes in all kinds of flavors, and you can pick whichever feels best for you. The flavors include lemon, for people who like a little kick of freshness. structured_data.articleBody:
At some point in your life, you’ll probably deal with bloating. Bloating happens when your belly feels tight or blown up like a balloon. It’s never fun. Most of the time, you’ll be dealing with it privately and no one will be able to tell that you feel like bursting out of your jeans. Sometimes, however, you might even experience your stomach sticking out and it’ll make you not want to leave the house.

The main causes of bloating are: 


 Constipation


 Stress and anxiety


 Irritable Bowel Syndrome 


 Gastroparesis 

While there’s no permanent cure for bloating and gas, there are plenty of remedies you can try to relieve your symptoms. One of the most popular things people try for bloating is apple cider vinegar. No, there is no concrete research on the subject, but apple cider vinegar has been a staple in almost every home remedy arsenal from sore throats to bloating. Let’s look at some of the benefits of apple cider vinegar for bloating and how it can help. 
What is Apple Cider Vinegar, Anyway? 
To start, you’ve surely seen apple cider vinegar on grocery store shelves. Sometimes recipes call for it, or maybe you avoid it because of its intense taste and sour smell. If you’re going to try apple cider vinegar for bloating, you need to understand what it is. 
Simply put, apple cider vinegar is the result of mixing apples and yeast together. The added years turn the sugar into alcohol during fermentation. The result is one of the most popular home remedies on the planet. 
Apple Cider Vinegar or ACV as we’ll call it for short has long been considered a home remedy for all sorts of ailments. Have back pain? ACV. Arthritis? ACV. Sore Throat? ACV. You get the picture. So, does it really work?
How is Apple Cider Vinegar Made?
If you’re interested in making your own apple cider vinegar for bloating, it’s actually pretty easy. There are only two steps. All you need to do is put slices of apples into water with yeast. When the apples are exposed to the yeast, they ferment and are turned into alcohol. 
As bacteria are added, the bacteria ferment the alcohol and turn it into acetic acid. Acetic is the main active ingredient in ACV. Acetic acid is what gives it such a strong smell and taste. Research suggests acetic acid is also what gives apple cider vinegar all those health benefits along with benefits for bloating. 
Benefits of Apple Cider Vinegar
ACV is Full of Healthy Stuff 
One of the main reasons apple cider vinegar is believed to have so many health benefits is that it contains acetic acid. It also contains good bacteria such as lactic, citric, and malic acids. These are all beneficial to the digestive system and your gut health. 
The Mother 
One thing to look out for if you’re buying apple cider vinegar is “The Mother.” Yes, we know it sounds a bit scary, but trust us it’s an important part of the process. You want your ACV to have this component. The mother is made up of proteins, enzymes, and good bacteria. Some ACV brands won’t have this, so make sure the one you buy does. 
Apple Cider Vinegar Can Kill Bacteria
Along with being a health remedy, ACV has long been used as a disinfectant. If you’re dealing with a nail fungus, wart, or skin infection, ACV can possibly help. 
It’s a Preservative
ACV is also a great preservative. Studies have shown that when used as a preservative in foods, it prevents bacteria such as E.coli from growing. It’s also natural, instead of other preservatives that may be harmful to you. 
It May Help with Acne
Using diluted ACV on your skin could also help clear up those pesky zits. If you are taking medication for acne or use prescription products, always consult with your doctor before trying apple cider vinegar for your acne. 
ACV May Help to Lower Blood Sugar 
Most research done on ACV has been in regards to managing Type 2 Diabetes. There have been several small studies that show consuming ACV can lower and regulate blood sugar levels. 
It’s important to remember there is not a lot of research regarding ACV, and all studies are anecdotal. If you are trying to treat a serious medical issue, always consult with your doctor. 
ACV May Help With Weight Loss 
There have also been studies that have shown ACV can help you lose weight. When you consume apple cider vinegar, it can increase your feeling of fulness so you’ll eat less. Now, keep in mind that on its own ACV is not a miracle weight loss supplement. You’ll need to continue maintaining a healthy diet and exercise if you want to potentially see a benefit from the apple cider vinegar.   
Benefits of Apple Cider Vinegar for Bloating 
Along with several health benefits, Apple Cider Vinegar may be good for bloating.  As with anything, it’s always important to consult with your doctor. For example, while it may help most people with bloating, ACV may make matters worse for people with type 1 diabetes or diabetic gastroparesis. In the study, those with the conditions saw a slowing in gastric emptying, instead of an improvement.   
If you don’t have either of those conditions, however, you should be able to see bloating improvements from apple cider vinegar. ACV can help aid in digestion because of the good bacteria in it. 
So, is apple cider vinegar good for bloating? The answer is that it might be. It depends on your microbiome and medical conditions. We cannot stress enough that you should always consult with a doctor before diving into a new home remedy for bloating such as apple cider vinegar.  
How to Take Apple Cider Vinegar for Bloating 
If you decide you want to see if you’ll get benefits from taking ACV, there are several ways to do so. Research suggests you should take around 1 tablespoon a day to see any kind of improvement. 
As we mentioned earlier, make sure if you’re buying pure ACV to get a brand that has “the mother.” This is what will help you get the most out of apple cider vinegar for bloating. Before you drink it, shake the bottle to make sure the mother is dispersed throughout the drink. If you aren’t crazy about drinking apple cider vinegar straight to help for bloating, you can always try other ways of adding it into your day.  
Add it to a Smoothie 
If you’re having trouble with the taste of ACV, throw it in a smoothie. You won’t be able to taste it that way. Try putting a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar into your favorite smoothie to start getting relief from bloating. 
Put it on a Salad
The tartness of apple cider vinegar is great on a salad. Mix it with some olive oil and you’re good to go. You can also make this mix and add it to egg salad, on a sandwich, or really anything you think it’ll taste good on. 
Apple Cider Vinegar Gummies
If pure ACV isn’t your jam, try Apple cider vinegar gummies for bloating. The Goli brand is very popular. If you go the gummy route, it’s recommended you take two a day. 
Put it in Tea
Another way to get your ACV on is to drink products that already provide health benefits such as prebiotics. That way, you don’t have to worry about masking the taste yourself. Try adding your ACV to a Halfday Tea Tonic to get your daily dose of apple cider vinegar, prebiotics, and plant fiber for bloating. It also tastes just like Snapple or Arizona Iced tea, just without the sugar, so you won't have to deal with that rough ACV taste. 

Conclusion
The bottom line is that apple cider vinegar can be good for bloating. The fermentation process fills the apple juice with good bacteria that are great for your gut. While there is not much research to back it up, it’s been a tried and true home remedy since the dawn of time. 
To try using apple cider vinegar for bloating, there are several ways to do so. Try it in tea, a gummy, or drink it straight. You can also add it to your favorite meals to mask the taste. Don’t be afraid of THE MOTHER and make sure you mix her up so you’re getting all the benefits!

No, there is no concrete research on the subject, but apple cider vinegar has been a staple in almost every home remedy arsenal from sore throats to bloating. Let’s look at some of the benefits of apple cider vinegar for bloating and how it can help. What is Apple Cider Vinegar, Anyway? To start, you’ve surely seen apple cider vinegar on grocery store shelves. Sometimes recipes call for it, or maybe you avoid it because of its intense taste and sour smell. If you’re going to try apple cider vinegar for bloating, you need to understand what it is. Simply put, apple cider vinegar is the result of mixing apples and yeast together. The added years turn the sugar into alcohol during fermentation. The result is one of the most popular home remedies on the planet. Apple Cider Vinegar or ACV as we’ll call it for short has long been considered a home remedy for all sorts of ailments. Have back pain? ACV. Arthritis? ACV. Sore Throat? ACV. You get the picture. So, does it really work? How is Apple Cider Vinegar Made? If you’re interested in making your own apple cider vinegar for bloating, it’s actually pretty easy. There are only two steps. All you need to do is put slices of apples into water with yeast. When the apples are exposed to the yeast, they ferment and are turned into alcohol. As bacteria are added, the bacteria ferment the alcohol and turn it into acetic acid. Acetic is the main active ingredient in ACV. Acetic acid is what gives it such a strong smell and taste. Research suggests acetic acid is also what gives apple cider vinegar all those health benefits along with benefits for bloating. Benefits of Apple Cider Vinegar ACV is Full of Healthy Stuff One of the main reasons apple cider vinegar is believed to have so many health benefits is that it contains acetic acid. It also contains good bacteria such as lactic, citric, and malic acids. These are all beneficial to the digestive system and your gut health. The Mother One thing to look out for if you’re buying apple cider vinegar is “The Mother.” Yes, we know it sounds a bit scary, but trust us it’s an important part of the process. You want your ACV to have this component. The mother is made up of proteins, enzymes, and good bacteria. Some ACV brands won’t have this, so make sure the one you buy does. Apple Cider Vinegar Can Kill Bacteria Along with being a health remedy, ACV has long been used as a disinfectant. If you’re dealing with a nail fungus, wart, or skin infection, ACV can possibly help. It’s a Preservative ACV is also a great preservative. Studies have shown that when used as a preservative in foods, it prevents bacteria such as E.coli from growing. It’s also natural, instead of other preservatives that may be harmful to you. It May Help with Acne Using diluted ACV on your skin could also help clear up those pesky zits. If you are taking medication for acne or use prescription products, always consult with your doctor before trying apple cider vinegar for your acne. ACV May Help to Lower Blood Sugar Most research done on ACV has been in regards to managing Type 2 Diabetes. There have been several small studies that show consuming ACV can lower and regulate blood sugar levels. It’s important to remember there is not a lot of research regarding ACV, and all studies are anecdotal. If you are trying to treat a serious medical issue, always consult with your doctor. ACV May Help With Weight Loss There have also been studies that have shown ACV can help you lose weight . You’ll need to continue maintaining a healthy diet and exercise if you want to potentially see a benefit from the apple cider vinegar. Benefits of Apple Cider Vinegar for Bloating Along with several health benefits, Apple Cider Vinegar may be good for bloating.  As with anything, it’s always important to consult with your doctor. For example, while it may help most people with bloating, ACV may make matters worse for people with type 1 diabetes or diabetic gastroparesis . In the study, those with the conditions saw a slowing in gastric emptying, instead of an improvement. If you don’t have either of those conditions, however, you should be able to see bloating improvements from apple cider vinegar. ACV can help aid in digestion because of the good bacteria in it. So, is apple cider vinegar good for bloating? The answer is that it might be. It depends on your microbiome and medical conditions. We cannot stress enough that you should always consult with a doctor before diving into a new home remedy for bloating such as apple cider vinegar. How to Take Apple Cider Vinegar for Bloating If you decide you want to see if you’ll get benefits from taking ACV, there are several ways to do so. Research suggests you should take around 1 tablespoon a day to see any kind of improvement. As we mentioned earlier, make sure if you’re buying pure ACV to get a brand that has “the mother.” This is what will help you get the most out of apple cider vinegar for bloating. Before you drink it, shake the bottle to make sure the mother is dispersed throughout the drink. If you aren’t crazy about drinking apple cider vinegar straight to help for bloating, you can always try other ways of adding it into your day. Add it to a Smoothie If you’re having trouble with the taste of ACV, throw it in a smoothie. You won’t be able to taste it that way. Try putting a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar into your favorite smoothie to start getting relief from bloating. Put it on a Salad The tartness of apple cider vinegar is great on a salad. Apple Cider Vinegar Gummies If pure ACV isn’t your jam, try Apple cider vinegar gummies for bloating. The Goli brand is very popular. If you go the gummy route, it’s recommended you take two a day. structured_data.articleBody:
We’ve been told since we were little that we should eat more fiber. Tired? Eat more fiber. Upset stomach? More fiber. No, this wasn’t a ploy to get you to eat more vegetables. Fiber is essential for a healthy digestive system, but why is that? 
Fiber is found in plants and is often referred to as the bulk material. That’s because our bodies cannot digest fiber, but it plays another role. Fiber, or dietary, fiber is an important part of any diet. It’s not too hard to get fiber into your diet since there are so many foods that contain it such as whole grains and many different fruits. 
Life gets busy and it can be hard to keep up with everything we’re supposed to include in our diet. One way to do that is to start drinking a high-fiber smoothie every day. Let’s look at what dietary fiber is, and how a high fiber smoothie can help improve your gut health. 
What is Dietary Fiber?
Dietary fiber is most commonly found in plants and is sometimes referred to as plant fiber. Fiber is a carbohydrate that can’t be digested. Typically carbohydrates are broken down and absorbed into your body as sugar molecules. Fiber is the part of the food that your body can’t digest, so other parts of your body can use it. 
When you intake fiber, it stays as-is for the most part. While it might sound like not being able to digest fiber is bad, it’s actually a very good thing and important for digestive health. Fiber regulates how your body uses sugar that it’s getting from other foods. It also works to manage your hunger and blood sugar, so it can help you lose weight. 
It’s suggested that children and adults both should be having at least 20 to 30 grams of fiber a day. The average American is usually only getting around 15 grams a day. There are two types of fiber, soluble ad insoluble fiber. 
Soluble Fiber  
Soluble fiber dissolves in water, so it will dissolve in your gut. It can help to slow down how quickly food is moving through your digestive system. Soluble fiber can also lower glucose levels and lower blood cholesterol.  
Foods With Soluble Fiber  


 Oatmeal


 Bananas


 Nuts


 Beans


 Lentils 


 Apples


 Blueberries 


Insoluble Fiber 
This type of fiber doesn’t dissolve in water, is referred to as roughage, and can help you stay regular if you’re dealing with constipation.
Foods With Insoluble Fiber 


 Wheat


 Whole wheat bread 


 Legumes 


 Brown rice


 Carrots


 Cucumbers 


 Tomatoes 


 Corn


Benefits of a High-Fiber Diet 
Fiber is important to your diet, and if you are experiencing problems like bloating, constipation, and other gut health-related issues you may want to try a high-fiber diet. There are many benefits to this type of diet. 
Weight Loss 
Increasing your fiber intake can help you lose weight. If you up your fiber intake to around 30 grams a day, you can shed quite a few pounds. This is because food that is high in fiber will keep you feeling full for longer. The fiber in the body will also keep you from absorbing higher amounts of calories from the foods you eat.
Once you lose weight, continuing a high-fiber diet can help you keep the pounds off, as well. Since fiber helps you stay full longer, you won’t be tempted to overeat, either.  
Lower Your Risk of Type 2 Diabetes 
A diet high in fiber can help you lower your risk of type 2 diabetes. According to a study done at Harvard, a diet low in fiber doubled the risk of type 2 diabetes. 
Reduce Constipation
Everyone has experienced constipation at least once, and it’s never fun. Drinking a high-fiber smoothie can help you relieve this gastrointestinal issue if you’re experiencing it commonly. 
Lower Your Risk of Heart Disease 
A diet high in fiber can also help lower your risk of heart disease. A Harvard study showed that those with a high dietary fiber intake had a 40% lower risk of heart disease. 
Fiber is Good for Gut Health
Your digestive system is home to trillions of good bacteria, often referred to as probiotics. The good bacteria in your gut help you maintain a healthy digestive system, and without them, you could have serious health problems. When you eat fiber, since you don’t digest it, it leaves food for the bacteria to eat and stay energized. Keeping the good bacteria well-fed will in turn keep your gut balanced and avoid issues such as bloating and constipation. 
Tips for Starting a High Fiber Diet 
If you’re ready to start a high-fiber diet, there are some things you should know. Here are some tips to help you get started. 
Start Slow 
When you start a high-fiber diet, it’s important to take it slow. Adding too much dietary fiber too quickly can make gastrointestinal issues worse. Add fiber into your diet gradually to avoid bloating and gas problems. 
Stay Hydrated 
Fiber is at its prime when you’re well-hydrated, so drink plenty of fluids when starting a high fiber diet. Not drinking enough fluids could result in constipation, or make matters worse if you’re already experiencing it. Drinking a high-fiber smoothie is a great way to make sure you’re staying hydrated while increasing your fiber intake. 
Eat Whole Grains
It’s important to check the ingredients when starting a high-fiber diet. Make sure that whole grains are at the top of the list. Opt for whole-grain bread, brown rice, and anything you can get your hands on that’s made with whole grains. 
Increase Your Fruit Intake 
Choose fruits that are high in fiber to add to your diet. They can also be enjoyed in a high-fiber smoothie! Fruits like apples, bananas, raspberries, and mangoes are great sources of fiber. While drinking a high-fiber smoothie is great, be sure to also eat fruits with the skins on them as well to get maximum fiber intake. 
High-Fiber Smoothies 
One way to start incorporating more fiber into your diet is to drink high-fiber smoothies. This is an easy way to get all your daily fiber in one fell swoop so you don’t have to worry about it the rest of the day. Green smoothies are one of the best types of high-fiber smoothies that you can drink. 
High fiber smoothies are jam-packed not only with fiber, but other essential nutrients you need throughout the day. They are typically a blend of fruits and vegetables and can be used as a dietary supplement. Drinking a high-fiber smoothie in the morning is a great way to get energized for the day while ensuring you’re getting the fiber you need.
The best part of making a high fiber smoothie at home is getting to put whatever you want in it. Typically, you should be adding things like spinach, kale, and other leafy greens for fiber. It’s important to be careful not to add too much sugar to your high fiber smoothie, as well. 
Foods to Put in Your High Fiber Smoothie 


 Berries such as blueberries, strawberries, and blackberries 


 Chia seeds 


 Bran 


 Nuts such as almonds 


 Leafy greens like spinach and kale 


 Adding a source of protein such as peanut butter and flaxseeds makes a high-fiber smoothie a perfect breakfast. You will also help yourself with hydration by drinking a high-fiber smoothie, as well. 
Start simple and choose your favorite fiber-rich fruits, leafy greens, and a protein source. Add milk, yogurt, or whatever you prefer and do some experimenting. There are also tons of blogs to check out online with high-fiber smoothie recipes to help you get started.  
Getting in the habit of drinking a high-fiber smoothie every day will help you improve your gut health and alleviate problems like bloating. It’s also a great way to make sure you’re having breakfast in the morning even if you don’t have time to sit down and have a meal.  
Other Tips for a High-Fiber Diet 
Along with your high-fiber smoothie, adding other foods to your diet can help you make sure you’re getting plenty of fiber and nutrients. Switch to whole grains in your bread, bagels and rice. You can also bake your own goods with whole grains to ensure a higher fiber content. 
If you’re a tea drinker, try Halfday Tea Tonics. Each can has 5g of plant fiber and is a healthier alternative to most commercial teas like Snapple and Arizona Iced Tea. They’re great for your gut health, too!
Conclusion
To sum it up, fiber is crucial if you want to improve your gut health. If you’re busy and find yourself unable to keep track, try a high fiber smoothie in the morning to make sure you’re getting your daily intake. 
Dietary fiber has many benefits including promoting weight loss, lowering the risk of Type 2 Diabetes, and promoting gut health. Making sure your gut is healthy will help you alleviate problems like constipation and bloating.  
High fiber smoothies are easy to make, and you can customize them however you’d like. All you need is leafy greens, high-fiber fruits, and a protein source. Try making one today!

structured_data.articleBody:
In addition to that lovely, warm Holiday smell, cinnamon provides a shocking number of health benefits. It can easily be incorporated across desserts and types of cooking, but Cinnamon Tea could be one of the easiest and best ways to get all the benefits from the spice. First, let's explore what exactly Cinnamon Tea is. 
What is Cinnamon Tea? 
Cinnamon (Cinnamomum Verum) is extracted from the heartwood of a Sri Lankan cinnamon tree. It twists up into rolls as it dries, forming the familiar cinnamon sticks that we use in cooking stuff. The sticks can also be pounded into a powder and used in various recipes or to brew tea like green tea with honey etc. Cinnamon is a fragrant, hearty, and full-bodied spice that has been used in conventional medicine for thousands of years, principally for stomach complications.
Cinnamon Tea – A prolific pool of health benefits 
Cinnamon tea has beneficial effects on human health & the mind. Varied cinnamons will have different chemical compositions, as well as different flavors and appearances. The number of valuable chemicals present will influence the possible health benefits. Nevertheless, they will all have indistinguishable improvements. All cinnamons contain procyanidins, catechins, and essential oils, among other substances.
Cinnamon's scent and flavor derive from cinnamaldehyde, predominantly found in the bark. Ceylon cinnamon, for instance, contains 49.9% cinnamaldehyde in its bark, whereas Chinese cinnamon can have up to 97 percent cinnamaldehyde. Let's take a deep dive into cinnamon tea’s health benefits.
Antioxidants
Cinnamon tea, like many peach green tea, cranberry black tea & other herbal teas, is profoundly high in antioxidants, which have health advantages for the body. Catechins and procyanidins are antioxidants found in cinnamon bark that safeguard bodily cells from being oxidized by free radicals.
Premature aging is also a result of them. Cinnamon bark also includes flavonoids and polyphenols, which protect the body from free radical oxidation.
Fresher Mouth Feel
Cinnamon is used in toothpaste and chewing gums for reasons other than its flavor. It might be able to assist you in getting rid of bad breath. Cinnamon has been shown in studies to have antifungal and antibacterial properties and to support in the battle against bacteria frequently found in the mouth that can cause tooth decay or gum disease. Cinnamaldehyde, the same molecule that gives cinnamon its flavor, has antimicrobial properties.
Reduce Blood Sugar Glucose 
Cinnamon is an admirable beverage for those with diabetes. Cinnamon has been revealed to behave in the body like insulin in many analyses. Insulin is a hormone that helps the body and tissues control sugar levels. 
Cinnamon assists in promoting insulin action and the prevention of insulin resistance in the body. Cinnamon was found to lower blood sugar levels in persons with type 2 diabetes in a study conducted by Thames Valley University in the United Kingdom. It has equal benefits, similarly derived from Halfday’s classic iced teas such as paleo friendly lemon black tea.
 

Improves Brain Health
Cinnamon has been shown to care for Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease. It could ease the reduction of oxidative stress and inflammation in the brain. 
According to the findings of a recent study, cinnamon tea consumption can productively improve cognitive processes. Insulin levels in the body can be readily regulated with increased memory. Cinnamon may also serve in the improvement of concentration, cognition, and intellectual skills.
Cinnamon tea should be used daily by those who desire to improve their cognitive capacities. Consequently, your memory will be more active, and your brain's control over bodily activities will be strengthened.
Body Pain and Rheumatoid Arthritis
Cinnamon has been discovered to lessen the progression of several major bone illnesses involving osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and bone metastases. The herb's phytochemical cinnamaldehyde stifles the progress of osteoclasts (cells that nibble at bones), diminishing bone deterioration and alleviating arthritic stings.
Cinnamon tea's benefits can be extended, as it helps to lessen the pain and swelling associated with the condition mentioned above. Ingest a pinch of cinnamon in powder form regularly to reap the anti-inflammatory effects of cinnamon tea, or apply a mixture of honey and cinnamon to the problematic area to relieve joint aches.
Weight-Loss Potential
Is it possible to lose weight by drinking cinnamon tea? Many obese people ask themselves this question & rely on naturally caffeine from green tea. Although there is relatively little research on the consequences of drinking cinnamon tea for weight loss, the few studies that have been undertaken on the topic have exhibited great ability.
According to a study conducted in India, ingesting 3g of cinnamon daily for 16 weeks will lead to weight loss and decrease your waist circumference. 
Cinnamon isolates produce browning of fat cells in the body, which is a practice that occurs when metabolism is heightened, according to another scientific study published in Scientific Reports. This suggests that cinnamon tea may improve weight loss and obesity prevention by increasing metabolism.
Alleviates Stomach Dilemmas
With a relaxing kiss of cinnamon, give your digestive system precisely what it needs. This mild spice can help to stimulate your digestive processes and get your system in tip-top shape. 
Due to the significant benefits that cinnamon provides, those who use cinnamon supplements are thought to have fewer gastrointestinal ailments such as bloating or gas, constipation. If you have IBS or wish to freshen up your digestive system, a cup of cinnamon tea & Halfday’s lemon black iced tea will make you feel better right away.
Anti-Inflammatory Effects
Ceylon cinnamon was discovered to be one of the top nutrients with exceptionally high anti-inflammatory qualities in a study. Reducing the risk of inflammation can promote your health in various habits. It will not only lower the chance of blood clots and other serious illnesses such as chronic diseases, but it will also lower soreness and swelling.
Reduced Cancer Risk 
When it comes to health and wellbeing, the big C is always a scary word. There has been numerous research examining the impact of cinnamon on cancer risk reduction, and all the evidence appears to trend accurately. Whereas the facts come from lab and animal experiments, the results suggest that cinnamon stimulates the formation of blood vessels in tumors, substantially slowing tumor growth.
Reduces the number of menstrual complications
Cinnamon tea is the remedy you've been looking for if you spend every month curled up in a fetal position and gripping your stomach. The effects of this spicy, vibrant drink on menstruation symptoms like PMS and discomfort have been examined. In one study, women who took 3 grams of cinnamon each day for the first three days of their period had less pain than those who took a placebo. So, the next time your period is due, make sure you have enough cinnamon and high-fiber cranberry black tea on hand.
Improves your skin health
Say bottoms up while raising a cup of cinnamon tea to have polished, younger-looking skin. This exquisite spice is high in antioxidants, which combat free radicals and lower the dangers linked with aging prematurely. Cinnamon, in addition to kicking off free radicals, promotes healthy blood flow, which gives your skin a boost of radiance by fostering new cell turnover. All of this, combined with its antibacterial and anti-inflammatory characteristics, means that simply sipping cinnamon can help you achieve healthy, balanced skin.
Healthy Hair
Cinnamon's proficiency to stimulate healthy blood flow also has the added benefit of improving your head health. A surge of blood to your scalp will strengthen and shine hair follicles. If you use cinnamon in your hair care routine, you'll notice that it has a gorgeous, robust perfume and can even illuminate your hair.

Reduces Cholestrol
Cinnamon tea is a plain recipe that may be made regularly to help lower LDL cholesterol levels in the body. This, in turn, serves to reduce the risk of heart disease, which can be lethal in the long term.
Promotes Healthy Bladder
Cinnamon's antibacterial and antifungal qualities are derived from the chemical eugenol and cinnamaldehyde, which treat urinary tract infections (urinary tract infections). It encourages the removal of toxins from the body system due to its diuretic characteristics. Cinnamon added to teas is a delicious way to consume its benefits, which can further be nourished with gluten free peach green tea
Cinnamon is revered in the world of spices for a reason. Because it is antibacterial, it contains a lot of phenols. Therefore, it can address a wide variety of ailments and general system issues. Organically grown cinnamon and other sorts of prebiotic teas are the ultimate for consumption. They also provide significantly more nutrients to the body than its inorganic counterparts. Explore Halfday's amazing range of classic iced teas including Green tea, Cranberry black tea, Lemon black, Peach green. Manufactured with lots of healthy plant fibers and pure ingredients without any extra calories or sugar, gives you the required energetic blow for your life.

Best Supplements for Bloating
 – Halfday Iced Tea
pages.description: Bloating sucks. Nothing worse than the tight pant feeling or general discomfort. Read more about supplements to take to beat the bloat.

structured_data.articleBody:
Being bloated is one of the most uncomfortable feelings to experience. It can strike at any time, too. There’s nothing worse than being out for a happy hour and wanting to unbutton your pants for sweet relief. Sometimes bloating is a minor problem, and other days you might feel like a balloon about to float away. Whatever the intensity, you surely don’t want to experience the dreaded bloat again. 
There are several ways to reduce bloating as well as prevent it altogether. Supplements, diet, and exercise are some of the top ways to beat the bloat. Before you run out and start popping anti-bloating pills, it’s important to get to the root cause of bloating and understand why it’s happening in the first place. Let’s look at what causes bloating, and the best supplements for bloating to help you stop puffing up. 
What is Bloating, Anyway?
To start, bloating is what happens when your gastrointestinal tract or GI tract for short is filled with air and gas. The gastrointestinal tract consists of the organs that anything you eat or drink travels through after you ingest them. The air trapped inside your GI tract will make you feel full and uncomfortable like you just ate the biggest burger on the planet. Sometimes, bloating can be so intense that you’ll physically see it in your stomach. 
Bloating is typically accompanied by pain in the stomach, excessive burping, and rumbling coming from your belly. Overall, it’s not fun to deal with especially if you have plans. In some instances, bloating happens alongside bloody stool, nausea, and vomiting. If you are experiencing frequent bloating and symptoms like this, call your doctor. 
There are quite a few ways that air can get trapped in your GI tract and cause bloating. Sometimes it’s because of the food you eat and will subside on its own later. Another common reason is swallowing air, which happens when you chew gum, smoke, or eat too fast. Eating too much can also cause bloating, and menstruation can increase the chances of bloating, as well. 
If you’re experiencing frequent bloating, it could be due to an underlying condition, so consult with your doctor if bloating is persistent. If no condition is found, you may be directed to alter your diet or take supplements for bloating. 
Best Supplements for Bloating 
Now that you know a little bit about bloating, there are supplements you can take to help alleviate your symptoms. Maintaining gut health is essential to avoid bloating and keep your digestive tract in good shape. Let’s look at some of the best supplements for bloating.
Digestive Enzymes 
Digestive enzymes are enzymes that occur naturally in the body, but can also be taken as a supplement. They are proteins that exist throughout your digestive system to help you break down the nutrients in the food you eat. There are three main types of digestive enzymes:

Amylases: Enzymes that breakdown carbs into simple sugars the body can use 
Lipases: Breaks down fat into usable fatty acids 
Proteases: Breaks down protein

When your digestive enzymes are at proper levels, you should have no digestive issues. Bloating can be a sign that your levels are low, and it’s time for a digestive enzymes supplement. They can be taken in pill form, and help you maintain a good level of digestive enzymes. There are plant and microbe-based supplements available, and vegan options depending on your preference. 
Ginger 
Ginger is one of the best digestive supplements for several ailments. It can help with an upset stomach and irregular bowel movements along with relieving bloat. It’s also full of antioxidants which are great for health, as well. Studies on ginger have shown that it can help speed up how fast your stomach empties which will help you avoid bloating. 
To utilize ginger for the gut health properties, it can be simply eaten as is. If you’re a sushi fan, gobble the ginger on your plate if you usually ignore it. It’s also good for cleaning the palette and preventing bacteria from the raw fish from bothering your system. If you don’t want to eat ginger, you can also take it as a pill supplement. Be careful not to take too much because it can have the opposite effect and cause heartburn. 
Peppermint Oil 
Peppermint oil is not only known for its delicious holiday smells. It’s also known for its anti-inflammatory properties because it’s rich in antioxidants. Peppermint oil also contains L-menthol, which can reduce muscle spasms in the GI tract, thus helping aid in gut health. If you have IBS, peppermint oil can help relieve symptoms. This makes it a great option to help you relieve your bloat. 
Vitamin D
Vitamin D is known to reduce the symptoms that come along with conditions like IBS, including bloating. Over 90% of people who have IBS will experience bloating at one point or another. Along with easing bloating, Vitamin D can reduce abdominal pain and constipation, which commonly happen alongside bloating. You can find Vitamin D supplements at your local pharmacy in various dosages to help find bloating relief. 
If you don’t want to take a capsule, vitamin D can be found in foods, as well. Egg yolks, some cheeses, and fatty fish are some of the top foods that have Vitamin D. They are also good sources of calcium. 
Cinnamon 
Cinnamon is rich in antioxidants and has properties that can help relieve that uncomfortable bloating. If you’ve had cinnamon, you know that it’s very flavorful and full of spices. The spices in cinnamon can help to reduce the pressure on your stomach caused by bloating and encourage the air and gas to move through you quickly. 
If you like chai, you can add cinnamon powder on top to increase the amount of cinnamon you’re ingesting. It’s also a great addition to smoothies or your coffee. You can also take cinnamon in pill form if you’re not crazy about the taste, but want to take one of the best supplements for bloating.
Probiotics 
Probiotics are bacteria that occur naturally in the gut. They are hands down one of the best supplements for bloating. When your gut is in proper working order, you won’t experience things like indigestion and bloating. When there are enough of them in your gut, they work to create a balance by attacking bad bacteria that has gotten into your GI tract. Probiotics are a fantastic thing to incorporate into your diet for gut health and to reduce the chance of dealing with bloating. Typically, we think of bacteria as a bad thing, but probiotics are good bacteria that help you maintain good gut health.

structured_data.articleBody:
Bloating is a common discomfort that everyone experiences. Whether it’s a snack that just didn’t feel right or more severe issues, bloating can disrupt your day-to-day. While there are short-term remedies on the market, to truly beat bloating, you need to start from your fundamental- your gut. Gut health and improving your microbiome is critical to solving bloating once and for all. 
Before you go into an Internet hole of gloom and doom self-diagnosing your bloating, let’s talk about gut health and natural remedies. There are many supplements and digestive aids on the market that can help, but small steps like adding tea and additional fiber to your daily routine can begin with immediate bloating reduction. 
What is Bloating? 
To start, bloating is what happens when you feel full and uncomfortable. You may even experience swelling in your abdomen that is visible. Typically, bloating is caused by a buildup of gas in the intestines after a meal. You feel full, tight, and overall totally unpleasant. Sometimes popping an antacid like Tums is enough, but other times it isn’t. 
While bloating is not life-threatening, the discomfort can feel like the end of the world, not to mention the pants just not fitting right. When you can’t find relief, you sit there full of gas feeling like a balloon. We get it, it sucks. Before trying the best tea for bloating, it’s important to understand the common causes and why you’re experiencing it. 
Gas 
The most common reason people experience bloating is too much gas built up in the intestine. Gas is a natural, unavoidable occurrence that is going to happen from time to time. Too much gas buildup, however, will result in bloating. Usually, if you eat too fast or drink a carbonated beverage, you can burp up the gas before it reaches your intestine, thus avoiding bloating. If you eat a large meal or you smoke, you are more likely to experience gas buildup that can lead to bloating. 
Indigestion 
Along with gas build-up, indigestion is a frequent culprit of bloating. Indigestion can be caused by drinking a lot of alcohol, eating a large meal, or NSAIDs like ibuprofen. If you are experiencing frequent periods of indigestion, it’s always best to consult a doctor to make sure nothing serious is going on.
Food Intolerance
To support gut health, it’s very important to be in tune with your body. Another reason many people experience bloating is food intolerance. For example, if you are lactose intolerant and eat dairy you may experience bloating. Gluten allergies and celiac disease can also cause intense bloating and fullness. This can usually be resolved by drinking an herbal tea for a bloated stomach. 
Constipation 
Constipation is another common cause of the dreaded stomach bloat. When you’re backed up, there’s nowhere for it to go and it can be very uncomfortable. This can be caused by a multitude of things such as a low fiber diet. 
Remedies 
 Bloating can be caused by a number of factors. Taking care of your gut health is essential if you want to eliminate the bloat. If you’re experiencing episodes of bloating due to gas, indigestion, or other reasons the good news is that herbal tea can help you reduce symptoms. So, let’s get into what types are the best tea for bloating.
Best Tea For Bloating 
Herbal teas are an excellent home remedy for stomach bloating. There are several options when it comes to herbal tea for bloating, so you’ll be sure to find a flavor you enjoy.
Peppermint Tea 
One of the best teas for bloating is peppermint tea. It’s not only a holiday drink, and the refreshing and minty flavor can be enjoyed year-round. Peppermint is known for its ability to ease digestive issues such as bloating due to flavonoids. Peppermint also relaxes the gut, which can ease unwanted pain and discomfort caused by bloating. 
Lemon 
If you’re looking to get rid of bloating quickly, lemon tea can help. All you really need is a slice of lemon and hot water. Lemon rinds contain d-limonene which has anti-inflammatory properties that can soothe your bloat. Lemon is also a diuretic, which can help your digestive system not to bloat to begin with. 
Ginger
Ginger tea is another fantastic tea for a bloated stomach. Ginger is a well-known remedy for upset stomach and nausea, so it should come as no surprise that a cup of ginger tea can help with bloating. In fact, a study in the World Journal of Gastroenterology showed the benefits of ginger on digestion. Ginger tea can help your digestive system move faster which can bring bloating relief quickly. 
Chamomile Tea
Chamomile tea is an herbal tea made from flowers in the Asteraceae family. This natural remedy has been used for centuries for various health conditions. Along with calming effects, the tea can eliminate water retention to help you get rid of bloating. If IBS is one of the things causing your bloating, chamomile tea can help you find relief. Chamomile tea is a great option if you are looking to avoid caffeine, as well.  
Gentian Root
Gentian root is derived from the Gentiana lutea plant. It has thick roots and yellow flowers. This tea will have a sweet taste but is followed by bitterness. If you plan to drink Gentian root tea for bloating, try mixing it with honey for a better taste. Gentian root is also used in bitters, commonly found in cocktails. 
Green Tea
Green tea has always been known for having incredible medicinal properties. That being said, it can also help get rid of stomach bloating due to high amounts of antioxidants. Green tea also contains catechins that help soothe the muscles in the gastrointestinal tract. Green tea improves the process of the digestive system to more effectively break down food, making it one of the best teas for bloating. 
 We all know green tea is one of the best teas for bloating because it’s loaded with antioxidants. Halfday's Green Tea with Honey & Ginseng has 8g of fiber and prebiotics to promote gut health and keep you from being bloated. It's non-carbonated to keep from creating unnecessary stomach issues.  

Black Tea 
Of all the best teas for bloating, black tea is never at the top of the list. This is because studies on black tea as beneficial for the gut are more recent than those on other teas. A study done at UCLA showed results that black tea can promote weight loss and other benefits by changing bacteria in the gut.  
The combination of black tea with cranberry juice concentrate works as a natural diuretic that can help resolve water retention. Black tea may alter energy metabolism in the liver and is linked to improving gut function and balancing the microbiome. Typically, green tea is the go-to for gut health, but these studies are showing that black tea may be the better choice.  
Not only is black tea great for the gut, but the Lemon Black Tea is also naturally caffeinated to give you a midday boost. This refreshing beverage combines the healing powers of black tea and lemon to make the perfect tea to help you reduce bloating. Halfday Lemon Black Tea is non-carbonated, so you don’t have to worry about bubbles upsetting your stomach. 
Conclusion
The bottom line is that bloating is not fun. When you are dealing with bloating, you want fast relief that is going to help your overall gut health. Drinking herbal tea is considered one of the best natural remedies for bloating. The great thing is there are several options to choose from when it comes to the best teas for bloating. 
 If you’re interested in trying some of the best teas for bloating, check out the selection at Halfday. All the teas are non-carbonated with added fiber to promote a healthy gut. Added sugar is all-natural, as well as caffeine. Halfday teas are also friendly to many diets such as gluten-free and paleo!

pages.description: Kombucha is a tea made from fermented green or black leaves. It has been consumed for thousands of years and, with its popularity and health benefits, is most likely to be consumed for a thousand more. This article provides a guide on the best times of the day to enjoy a healthy cup of Kombucha.

headings.text: Best Time to Drink Kombucha - Find Out the Truth!
Right after Waking Up in the Morning:

structured_data.articleBody:
All tea-lovers or people even mildly interested in teas or drinks made out of leaves have heard of Kombucha due to the amazing health benefits it provides. Kombucha is preferred over tea by some due to having more beneficial prebiotics by tea. This effervescent drink has been known from ancient times to today for killing harmful bacteria inside the body, improving the immune system, being an excellent anti-inflammatory drink, and being rich in antioxidants that will enhance an individual's overall health. It is considered an amazing detox drink that cleanses the body and digestive tract of the drinker. The process of fermentation prepares kombucha. Bacteria, yeast, and sugar are added in specific proportions in the green tea or black tea leaves and left to ferment for more than a week. At the end of the process, a mushroom-like semi-liquid is formed on the surface of the fermented tea; this semi-liquid is then used to make Kombucha. This drink is produced through fermentation; the tea naturally contains a very minute amount of alcohol, around only 1%.
The taste of Kombucha:
The reason that Kombucha is not as popular as a tea in most parts of the World, despite carrying more health benefits than regular black or green tea, is because of its distinct taste. The earthy and herb-like flavor that you might enjoy with black or green tea is not found in Kombucha; instead, due to the process of fermentation that produces lactic acid, Kombucha tastes a bit sour and simply put; it is not everyone's cup of tea. Especially to people that like sweet teas, Kombucha tastes very sour. It is an acquired taste, and most drinkers also add a dash of sweet juice to the drink to neutralize its sour flavor. However, due to its sour taste that comes from its acidic properties, a Kombucha is a perfect tea blend with the lowest residual sugar levels and highest prebiotic properties—making it an ideal cup of tea for health enthusiasts.
 


Best time to drink Kombucha:
One of the most popularly asked questions about this drink is when is the best time to drink Kombucha.
It is a herbal, effervescent, healthy drink that can be drunk throughout the day at different timings. However, excessive consumption of anything is never good, and hence one should only stick to 1-3 cups a day. There is no strict schedule of what time of the day you can enjoy a healthy and delicious cup of this bubbly fermented tea. Due to its health benefits and good nutrient composition, you can enjoy it any time of the day. Nevertheless, here are some of the best times to enjoy your Kombucha and feel refreshed/recharged.
 


Right after Waking Up in the Morning:
Mornings signify the start of your day, and nothing seems more tempting on a morning than a few extra minutes of comfortable sleep. To help freshen your mind and activate your body, Kombucha works like the perfect healthy drink. The low caffeine concentration in the Kombucha acts as an ideal pump of energy that the mind and body require early in the morning, without it being too much caffeine in your system, like in the cases of concentrated solid coffee or black tea. There has been little research on the benefits of Kombucha that shows that drinking Kombucha on an empty stomach acts as a great detoxifying drink and helps balance the bacteria in the gut, which helps in a systematic and smooth digestive process throughout the day.
Many people prefer a cold beverage in the morning to refresh them from the inside, especially on summer mornings; in such cases, a cold tea like that of HalfDay is a great recharging, cold, and healthy option to drink. The canned iced tea is available in 4 delicious flavors; Peach Green, Lemon Black, Green Tea with Honey and Ginseng, and a limited edition Cranberry Tea flavor.
 

 
 
With your Meals:
Many people prefer drinking fizzy soft drinks with their food instead of water. Kombucha works as a healthy and delicious alternative to these fizzy soft drinks. It is a highly healthy choice compared to artificially flavored fizzy soft drinks, is made from the natural process of fermentation, is rich in prebiotics and antioxidants, and aids with digestion and detoxification. Making it a perfect drink to be drunk along with meals.
Post-exercise or workout sessions:
Most bodies crave an energy recharge after a workout, and hence many people resort to sugary drinks post-workout that recharge their bodies and provide them with the energy to continue with the day. Kombucha is made from organic tea and contains antioxidants, prebiotics, and organic acids, that help rehydrate the tired body after a workout and eliminate the need for a sugary drink. Kombucha replenishes the body while providing good health benefits and is an overall safer and healthier alternative to post-workout beverages. The small amount of caffeine found in the drink also helps the body regain its energy and continue with the day.
Middle of the Day:
Midday blues are a widespread occurrence, where a person wants nothing more than to be done with their day and head back to the comfort of their house to relax, yet a lot of activities for the day are yet to be completed. Hence, the body requires something to recharge the mind and the physical energy. Most people end up eating a sugary snack and then feeling guilty afterward. An iced cup of Kombucha can serve as a deliciously recharging treat for the mind and the body, without the guilt of consuming extra sugar or unhealthy carbs. A cup of Kombucha will rehydrate the body and re-energize it by providing a healthy dose of antioxidants and a minute amount of caffeine and sugar in the system to continue with the day. The digestive properties of Kombucha keep the gut healthy and the person feeling lighter and fresher.

Before Bedtime:
Night cravings are super intense for most individuals. Most of us end up resorting to unhealthy and sugary drinks or snacks right before bedtime, only to feel guilty about unhealthy eating habits and nighttime snacks later. If you are not highly sensitive to caffeine and low levels of caffeine won't disrupt your sleeping pattern, satisfying your nighttime craving with a cup of Kombucha instead of unhealthy snacks is the way to go! Not only is it a low-calorie, healthy option, but it will also detoxify your gut and improve digestion, helping you sleep better and have a refreshing day in the morning. Find the flavor and concentration of kombucha that works the best for you and add it to your lifestyle for a healthier lifestyle
A deliciously healthy drink:
Enjoy the benefits of various types of tea with the delicious and refreshing canned iced teas by HalfDay. Available in 4 different flavors, HalfDay’s iced tea is one of the healthiest drink options to add to your lifestyle.  With high levels of prebiotic fiber that work like a charm for improved gut health, low sugar levels, low calories, natural caffeine from organic tea leaves, and gluten-free, a can of this iced tea is bound to be the perfect healthy drink to add to your lifestyle for an improved body and mind health, along with a refreshed outlook. It is available in four delicious flavors to cater to different taste buds, lemon black tea, peach green tea, green tea with honey and Ginseng, and Cranberry black tea.
