headings.text: Amount of Caffeine In Different Teas

structured_data.articleBody:
When you need some pep in your step, you probably turn to caffeine. Coffee lovers hold their energizing bean water closer to their hearts than some of the people in their lives. Coffee is so popular that in 2020/2021 about 166.63 million 60 kilogram bags of coffee were consumed all over the world. That’s a lot of beans! While delicious and helpful during the workday, there can definitely be too much of a good thing. Coffee can also make you super jittery, so tea is usually a better option when it comes to caffeine. If you want to lower your intake, it might be best to switch to tea and try something like Snapple.

 
Snapple has been a staple for tea lovers since the 1970s, but the question is does it have caffeine? Well, it depends on the type of Snapple you’re drinking. Let’s dive into whether Snapple actually does have caffeine and how it works. 
What is Caffeine?
Before we dive into whether Snapple does have caffeine, we need to talk about caffeine itself first. Caffeine is a natural stimulant found in over 60 plants, including:  


 Coffee Beans 


 Tea Leaves 


 Kola Nuts 


 Cacao Pods

When you’re looking for a caffeine source, most people reach for coffee or tea. Drinking it is one of the easiest ways to get it into your body, and it tastes good too! Caffeine is so popular that around 80% of the world consumes some sort of caffeine product every day.

Once you ingest caffeine, it gets to work right away. It’s absorbed into the bloodstream by the guy to give you the energy boost you’ve been craving. It then moves into the liver and is broken down so it can move around your body. 
Caffeine works by stimulating the central nervous system, which causes you to feel more awake. It’s also a diuretic, which means it helps your body to get rid of extra salt and water by making you pee more often. The biggest draw to caffeine is the fact that it makes us more alert and gets us through the day if we’re feeling tired. 
Whenever you’re feeling tired, a little caffeine should do the trick. The recommended daily amount for adults is around 400 milligrams. If you drink more than that, you may experience: 


 Insomnia


 Headaches


 Nervousness


 Irritability 


 Frequent Urination


 Increased Heartrate 


 Muscle Tremors 

If you’ve ever drank way too much coffee in a day, you know what it feels like. It can be unpleasant and keep you up, resulting in needing, even more, to get you going the next day. It can be a vicious cycle if you let it. 
Caffeine and Gut Health 
Before seeing if Snapple does in fact have caffeine, we need to look at caffeine's effect on the gut, too. There is some debate on how caffeine affects gut health. Typically, it depends on the source that it’s coming from. For example, coffee can lead to an increase of stomach acid which can cause bloating, gas, and heartburn.  
Since caffeine is a stimulant, it activates your digestive tract. Have you ever noticed that after you have your morning Starbucks you need a bathroom run shortly after? Caffeine is good at helping to keep you regular and can also aid in constipation if you’re having problems in that area.  
As far as your gut health is concerned, research shows that people who consume caffeine have a more diverse microbiome. If you’re consuming tea with caffeine, you’ll also get the gut health benefits of tea such as a decrease in inflammation, and reduced risk of diseases such as diabetes. 
Caffeine in Tea 
Caffeine occurs naturally in the tea plant, Camellia Sinensis. The amount of caffeine in your tea will ultimately depend on the brew time and temperature of the water. For example, green and white teas will have less caffeine than black teas because they are brewed for less time and in cooler water.  
Do you feel jittery after you drink a cup of coffee? Switching to tea can stop that. This is because tea contains L-theanine. Tea is the only plant that contains L-theanine which is an amino acid that promotes a calm mind and relaxation. When it’s combined with the caffeine in the tea you will be alert, but without all that sweaty shaking you get when you chug a cold brew from Starbucks.

 White Tea: 10-15mg


 Green Tea: 15-30mg 


 Black Tea: 60-75mg 


 Matcha: 60-80mg

Snapple also doesn’t add extra caffeine and only contains what naturally occurs in tea. They generally use black tea in their products, which has a high concentration of caffeine, but still not as much as a cup of coffee.  
Snapple tea products contain 2.31 mg of caffeine per fluid ounce. So, a standard 16oz bottle is going to have around 37mg of caffeine. This is a lot lower than a cup of coffee, and well below the safe amount of caffeine, you can have daily. 
Does Diet Snapple Have Caffeine? 
We’ve been trained to believe that if a product is labeled ‘diet’ that it’s better for you. Does that mean Diet Snapple doesn’t have caffeine? Not necessarily.  
In fact, if you look at the chart on this page, you’ll see that Diet Snapple can actually have more caffeine. Diet Snapple Peach Tea does have a little more caffeine than the regular Snapple Peach, but not much. A 16oz bottle of Diet Peach Snapple contains 38mg of caffeine, instead of 37. For comparison, there is about 90mg of caffeine in the same size coffee.  
You’ll be able to find the caffeine content on the labels of the Diet Snapple Tea so you can whether it does or doesn’t fall into how much you want to have. It’s also important to note that a 16oz bottle of Snapple Tea is two servings. 
Should You Drink Snapple?
Even though Snapple Tea does have a lower caffeine amount than coffee, there are several reasons to find an alternative. Snapple is full of sugar and other additives. If you drink Diet Snapple, it contains aspartame, which is notoriously bad for you. 
Snapple Alternatives
To keep your caffeine intake low and your gut happy, try Haldfay Tea Tonics. We recommend the Peach Green Tea as an alternative to Snapple. You’ll get all the pick-me-up perks of natural caffeine from the green tea without all the junk.

 
You can also make your own tea at home so you know exactly what you’re getting. That way, you have control over all of the ingredients and can brew the tea as strong or not as strong as you like! You’ll never have to stand in the aisle wondering whether or not Snapple does or doesn’t have caffeine. 
Conclusion
The bottom line is yes, Diet Snapple Tea does contain caffeine. It’s a lower amount than a cup of coffee, but it’s full of sugar and other not great things that won’t help your gut. Drinking other tea options will help you avoid gas, bloating, and other problems.

structured_data.articleBody:
Ginseng is a buzzword in the healthy product community, and you’ve likely had it at some point in your life. It’s a popular natural herb throughout Asia and North America that has many medicinal properties. It’s typically mixed into other products like candy and tea, which leaves people wondering, what does ginseng actually taste like?  

Well, the thing is that unless you buy and prepare your own, you may never know. Ginseng is masked by other flavors in tea and other products because it’s very bitter. While some people love bitter tastes, others may not be crazy about it. So, let’s look at ginseng and answer the question ‘what does it taste like?’
What is Ginseng? 
To start, we need to go over what ginseng actually is. The word ginseng is slapped onto labels of lots of products including energy drinks, candy, and tea. Most people don’t take the time to look into what something is, and knowing it’s supposed to be healthy is usually enough to get you to buy it.  
Ginseng is a plant that grows in North America and Asia and is harvested for its root. That’s where all the health benefits come from. It's a light-colored root that’s shaped like a fork with oval-shaped leaves. It’s been used as a natural remedy for various health issues for centuries. 
Health Benefits of Ginseng 
Before we get into figuring out what ginseng actually does taste like, it’s important to understand the health benefits. While there isn’t a lot of concrete research on the benefits, ginseng has been a trusted medicinal remedy all over the world for a long time. There are 11 different varieties, so depending on which you choose the potency can be different. This can alter how beneficial ginseng can be as far as health benefits go. Before using ginseng to try to treat a medical issue at home, always consult with your doctor. 
Ginseng Can Give You an Energy Boost 
The most common place you’re going to find ginseng is tea and energy drinks. For example, Monster Energy lists ginseng as one of its top ingredients on the can. It’s also right on the front of AriZona Beverage Company’s green tea products.  
Research has shown that ginseng promotes an increase in energy, so it’s a great companion to caffeine. If you deal with chronic fatigue, adding ginseng to your diet can help you naturally increase your energy levels, as well. 
It Can Help Regulate Blood Sugar 
Ginseng may also lower and regulate blood sugar levels to treat diabetes. You don’t have to have diabetes to utilize ginseng for blood sugar regulation. In fact, incorporating ginseng into your diet could help you curb sugar cravings. Research has shown that ginseng can improve pancreatic cell function and insulin production, which can help your body with sugar absorption into tissue so there is less build-up. 
It May Boost Immunity 
In the world we’re living in, any little bit of immunity-boosting can help. Ginseng can help increase immunity, so adding it to your diet won’t hurt. 
Helps You Focus 
Since ginseng is typically found in caffeinated products like tea, it should come as no surprise that it can help you focus. There is evidence from research that shows ginseng can give you a short-term boost in concentration. So, grabbing a tea with ginseng for your study session may help you get that paper finished on time. 
Reduces Inflammation 
If you have arthritis or other inflammatory conditions, you may not care about what ginseng tastes like, but what does it do for your body? When dealing with chronic inflammation in your joints or other parts of the body, you know how painful it can be. Ginseng is full of antioxidants and anti-inflammatory properties which can aid in reducing inflammation. Studies have shown that ginseng extracts could potentially stop inflammation in its tracks and increase antioxidant capacities. 
What Does Ginseng Taste Like?
Now, to answer the burning question of ‘what does ginseng taste like?’ There’s a good chance if you’re reading this you’ve never had ginseng on its own. Since it’s usually added to other products, the taste of ginseng is typically masked very well. In fact, there is research that shows companies intentionally mask the taste of ginseng because of how bitter it is. 
So, what does ginseng taste like? Well, it’s a root so ginseng is going to have a woody taste along with other flavors. Think about ginger, ginseng looks similar and has the same type of texture. 
On its own, ginseng is extremely bitter with sweet undertones that can be hard to notice. When it’s completely raw, many people don’t enjoy the taste. The root texture can also be hard to deal with since it’s difficult to chew.  
You can also get dried ginseng which will be chewy. The problem is that if it’s really dry, it can be too hard to chew and unmanageable. If you cook ginseng, it can become creamy but it’s very easy to overcook it. When it’s overcooked, ginseng turns into a pile of mush. The texture of ginseng is a big reason why you don’t see it in a lot of cooking recipes. 
Does Ginseng Taste Like Ginger?
We’ve compared ginseng to ginger as far as appearance and texture go, but what about taste? Even though they are both roots, ginseng does not taste like ginger. If you’ve had ginger, you know it has a very distinct flavor. It’s spicy and can be overpowering if you use too much of it in a dish. Ginseng doesn’t have the spicy taste to it as ginger does, just the powerful bitterness. Sometimes you’ll find ginger and ginseng in the same products, which can make it easy to assume they taste the same. 
How to Use Ginseng
Now that you know all about what ginseng tastes like and what it does for you, it’s time to add it to your diet. Cooking with ginseng is not ideal, especially if you’re starting out. Your best bet with ginseng is going to be drinking it in tea or taking a supplement. When you take ginseng supplements, make sure to read the directions on the bottle because some of them require you to take them with food while others may not. Again, always consult with your doctor before adding a new supplement to your diet. 
Ginseng Products 
If you’re new to ginseng but want to incorporate it into your diet, try tea first. You can purchase teas that have ginseng in them, but it’s important to look at the ingredient list. Companies like AriZona Beverage Company have gotten in trouble in the past for advertising ginseng in their green tea when there actually wasn’t any in it.  
We know you’re busy, so finding ginseng and preparing it for tea on your own might not be in the cards. Don’t worry, there are options out there that aren’t sugary energy drinks!
Ginseng Tea 
There are plenty of teas on the market that advertise ginseng as the main ingredient, but when you read the fine print you’ll find that there isn’t much in there. To be sure you’re getting a good amount of ginseng, we recommend Half Day’s Geen Tea with Honey and Ginseng. It tastes just as good as other brands without all the junk. Along with the benefits of ginseng, you’ll get 5g of plant fiber that provide prebiotics to feed the good bacteria in your gut!

Ginseng Supplements 
Another great way to incorporate ginseng into your diet is to take dietary supplements. We recommend Care/Of focus supplements from Target. They’re gluten-free, non-GMO and vegan so you know you’re getting the good stuff.  
Conclusion
If you were looking to figure out what ginseng actually does taste like, you came to the right place. We’re glad you didn’t run out and buy a ginseng root to try cooking with it because that bitterness can be a real bummer. The good news is there are plenty of healthy options for getting ginseng into your diet that mask the taste!

It Can Help Regulate Blood Sugar Ginseng may also lower and regulate blood sugar levels to treat diabetes. You don’t have to have diabetes to utilize ginseng for blood sugar regulation. In fact, incorporating ginseng into your diet could help you curb sugar cravings. Research has shown that ginseng can improve pancreatic cell function and insulin production, which can help your body with sugar absorption into tissue so there is less build-up. There is evidence from research that shows ginseng can give you a short-term boost in concentration. So, grabbing a tea with ginseng for your study session may help you get that paper finished on time. headings.text: History of the Arnold Palmer and Alternatives for a Gut-Friendly Diet

structured_data.articleBody:
Summer is fast approaching and that means it’s time for refreshing patio drinks like an ice-cold Arnold Palmer. While you may want to throw caution to the wind and chug as many sugary drinks as you can, think of your gut! The solution is as easy as grabbing a diet Arnold Palmer instead of a regular, right? Well, not exactly.  

If you’re unfamiliar, an Arnold Palmer is a half tea half lemonade drink that’s a total crowd-pleaser. You can even add a shot of vodka to it and call it a John Daily. The most popular brand you’re going to find is the AriZona Tea Company’s diet Arnold Palmer. This drink, however, is not very gut-friendly and is loaded with artificial sweeteners. So, let’s look at what’s in a diet Arnold Palmer, and healthy alternatives to keep you from bloating this summer!
What is an Arnold Palmer?
To start, the Arnold Palmer is a drink named after the famous golfer. It’s a half and half mixture of unsweet black tea and lemonade. The combination creates a refreshing taste that’s not too sweet and not too sour. It’s perfect for summer and once you try one you’ll want to chug at least three more. 
History of the Arnold Palmer 
The reason for the namesake is that Arnold Palmer actually created the drink. Before Arnold Palmer became a drink mogul, he was a professional golfer that was very well known. He’s also regarded as being one of the most charming golf players in history, so even people who didn’t care for golf were fans of this guy. Palmer won many events on the PGA Tour and was nicknamed ‘The King.’ 
Palmer was so well-known because his career took off right around the time that television was becoming a staple in people’s homes in the 1950s. So, on top of his golf career, Arnold Palmer was a household name and is credited with assisting in making golf as popular as it is today. 
Flash forward to the 1960s while Arnold Palmer is out to lunch one day. Palmer was about to order lunch after a long morning at the golf course in Palm Springs. He decided to order a mix of half tea and half lemonade, which was something his wife had been making for him for years. 
Someone at another table heard him order this and thought it sounded delicious. So, they decided to order what Arnold Palmer was having and the drink was born. Arnold Palmer had no idea how popular the drink would become after that. 
It wasn’t until 1997 that the drink was mentioned nationally. The Arnold Palmer was mentioned in the Rolling Stone hot issue, which continued to increase its popularity. In 2001, Palmer partnered with the AriZona Beverage Company to begin bottling the drink under his namesake.  
The drink continued to be so popular that in 2012 ESPN did a 30 for 30 Shorts documentary on it that featured Arnold Palmer himself.  
Arnold Palmer’s face continues to grace the shelves of convenience stores on giant cans of the delicious beverage. So, when you’re craving the refreshing beverage, you’re likely to reach for a can of diet Arnold Palmer from AriZona. 
Arnold Palmer Variations 
Along with the original Arnold Palmer, there are several variations of the drink. 
Winnie Palmer 
Winnie Palmer was Arnold Palmer’s first wife. This variation of the drink simply uses sweet tea instead of unsweetened tea. Keep in mind this one is going to up your sugar intake! 
John Daily
This one is for when you’re feeling boozy. It’s a traditional Arnold Palmer with a shot of vodka thrown into it. You can play with the number of ingredients to get the taste exactly to your liking. MillerCoors sells a malt-based version of this concoction under the name Arnold Palmer Spiked. 
AriZona Arnold Palmer Ingredients
Since one of the main ingredients in an Arnold Palmer is tea, it should be healthy right? Well, it depends on where you’re getting it from. AriZona sells two versions of the drink, and one is a Diet Arnold Palmer. This version is ideally supposed to be healthier for you, but it’s important to look at the ingredients. 
Arnold Palmer 
When you examine a can of Arnold Palmer, the third ingredient is high fructose corn syrup. We all know that this is not good for you. High fructose corn syrup is a common sweetener in sodas and other drinks such as the Arnold Palmer from AriZona. While it’s similar to sugar, high fructose corn syrup gives you extra calories and can cause weight gain.
Diet Arnold Palmer 
The diet version of Arnold Palmer eliminates the high fructose corn syrup, but it’s still not just tea and lemonade. In fact, the high fructose corn syrup is replaced with ingredients like sucralose Advertised as half tea and half lemonade, the AriZona Arnold Palmer includes several other ingredients such as sucralose which can alter your gut microbiome.  
According to the National Library of Medicine, the consumption of sucralose can decrease the number of good bacteria in your gut, which we already know can cause a number of problems. So, even though the word ‘diet’ should mean you’re getting a healthier version of an Arnold Palmer, the added ingredients could do you more harm than good. You may be better off making your own diet Arnold Palmer at home! 
Healthy Diet Arnold Palmer Alternatives
One of the best ways to ensure you’re not putting anything you don’t need into your body is to make it yourself! The good news is that a diet Arnold Palmer is easy to replicate, and you can tailor it to taste exactly how you want it to!
Homemade Diet Arnold Palmer Ingredients 
All you need to make your own diet Arnold Palmer is tea and lemonade, it’s super easy. Before you run out and buy whatever tea and lemonade are on the shelf, keep your gut in mind. Part of the reason you’re choosing to make this at home is to avoid all of the nasty junk that’s in the canned version, so it’s important to be mindful of the ingredients of what you’re using. 
Your best bet will be to brew your own tea and make your own lemonade. We understand that’s not always an option, and you might want to throw something together in a pinch. For lemonade, we definitely recommend making your own at home. Store-bought lemonade is always packed full of sugar and other unnecessary ingredients. We recommend this gut-friendly lemonade recipe with apple cider vinegar for an extra health kick.  
As for tea, using organic black tea is going to be best. If you like sweetener, you can use a little bit but the combination of the lemonade and the unsweet tea should be enough to get your fix. If you don’t want to mess with brewing your own tea, we recommend HalfDay’s Lemon Black Tea.


 
The extra citrus from the lemon will give your diet Arnold Palmer an extra kick, and there’s no added junk to this tea. There’s only 3g of sugar, so you can feel good about adding it to your summer bev’s. All you need to do is shake the can, pour it in, and you’re ready to go.  
For a recipe, the general rule of thumb is to add half tea and half lemonade over ice. Stir, and you’re done. Arnold Palmer preferred to do two-thirds tea and one-third lemonade, so have some fun playing around with what works best for you. To really bring the drink together, you can add a fresh lemon wedge and a cute straw. 
Conclusion
The bottom line is that a diet Arnold Palmer is delicious. The problem is that when you get the canned version, you are going to be drinking a lot of sugar and other additives. Making your own diet Arnold Palmer at home will help you ensure you know exactly what’s in your drink! Try one with Halfday’s Lemon Black Tea, today!

While it’s similar to sugar, high fructose corn syrup gives you extra calories and can cause weight gain. Diet Arnold Palmer The diet version of Arnold Palmer eliminates the high fructose corn syrup, but it’s still not just tea and lemonade. In fact, the high fructose corn syrup is replaced with ingredients like sucralose Advertised as half tea and half lemonade, the AriZona Arnold Palmer includes several other ingredients such as sucralose which can alter your gut microbiome . According to the National Library of Medicine, the consumption of sucralose can decrease the number of good bacteria in your gut, which we already know can cause a number of problems. So, even though the word ‘diet’ should mean you’re getting a healthier version of an Arnold Palmer, the added ingredients could do you more harm than good. You may be better off making your own diet Arnold Palmer at home! Healthy Diet Arnold Palmer Alternatives One of the best ways to ensure you’re not putting anything you don’t need into your body is to make it yourself! The good news is that a diet Arnold Palmer is easy to replicate, and you can tailor it to taste exactly how you want it to! Homemade Diet Arnold Palmer Ingredients All you need to make your own diet Arnold Palmer is tea and lemonade, it’s super easy. Before you run out and buy whatever tea and lemonade are on the shelf, keep your gut in mind. Part of the reason you’re choosing to make this at home is to avoid all of the nasty junk that’s in the canned version, so it’s important to be mindful of the ingredients of what you’re using. Your best bet will be to brew your own tea and make your own lemonade. We understand that’s not always an option, and you might want to throw something together in a pinch. For lemonade, we definitely recommend making your own at home. Store-bought lemonade is always packed full of sugar and other unnecessary ingredients. We recommend this gut-friendly lemonade recipe with apple cider vinegar for an extra health kick. As for tea, using organic black tea is going to be best. If you like sweetener, you can use a little bit but the combination of the lemonade and the unsweet tea should be enough to get your fix. If you don’t want to mess with brewing your own tea, we recommend HalfDay’s Lemon Black Tea . The extra citrus from the lemon will give your diet Arnold Palmer an extra kick, and there’s no added junk to this tea. There’s only 3g of sugar, so you can feel good about adding it to your summer bev’s. All you need to do is shake the can, pour it in, and you’re ready to go. For a recipe, the general rule of thumb is to add half tea and half lemonade over ice. Stir, and you’re done. Arnold Palmer preferred to do two-thirds tea and one-third lemonade, so have some fun playing around with what works best for you. To really bring the drink together, you can add a fresh lemon wedge and a cute straw. Conclusion The bottom line is that a diet Arnold Palmer is delicious. The problem is that when you get the canned version, you are going to be drinking a lot of sugar and other additives. Making your own diet Arnold Palmer at home will help you ensure you know exactly what’s in your drink! Try one with Halfday’s Lemon Black Tea , today! Back to blog

headings.text: Inulin Sweetener: What Is It, and How Do You Use It?
Inulin Sweetener May Help With Other Health Concerns
Why Should You Replace Sugar with Inulin Sweetener?

structured_data.articleBody:
Everyone has heard of natural sweeteners to replace sugar in your diet. There are key players such as honey and stevia, but have you heard of inulin sweeteners? Inulin has been around for centuries and occurs naturally, but has recently become a popular sweetener option for those looking to lower their sugar intake.  
Having too much sugar in your diet can lead to all sorts of problems from inflammation to boating and an unbalanced gut microbiome. Replacing sugar in your diet can help you kick your sweets habit and get you to enjoy less sugary foods in general. 

Adding a sweetener like inulin to your diet is a great option because it’s also dietary fiber. This means you’re replacing sugar with a substitute that has many health benefits to it other than just getting rid of the sugar. So, let’s dive into what inulin is and how you can use it as a sweetener. 
What is Inulin?
Inulin is a naturally occurring dietary fiber. It was approved by the FDA as a dietary fiber in 2018, so it’s still relatively new as far as mainstream food goes.  It can be found in several fruits and veggies, with the highest concentration found in chicory root. Inulin is a soluble dietary fiber, so it dissolves in water and can aid in digestion problems.  
We all know that fiber is great for your digestive system, and many fruits and veggies give us fiber naturally. Soluble fiber is the kind that dissolves in water, which means it can help slow down digestion, keep you full longer and help balance your blood sugar and cholesterol. 
Inulin is also a fructan. A fructan is a chain of fructose molecules that connects in a way that makes it so the intestine can’t break them down, making it a prebiotic. This means that they are able to travel to the lower gut. When they get there, they become food for the good bacteria living in your gut, otherwise known as probiotics.  
Since prebiotics are unable to be digested by the body, they stay in your gut. While it may sound like a not great thing to have organisms lingering around in your stomach, it is. This is because prebiotics provide probiotics the energy they need to keep your gut healthy. Without them, you’d be dealing with bloating and all sorts of digestive problems. If you’re interested in learning more about prebiotics and probiotics, check out this article.   
Inulin is a starchy carbohydrate substance sound in various plants such as:  


 Wheat


 Onions


 Bananas


 Artichokes


 Asparagus 

The most common source of inulin is chicory root. Chicory root is a leafy plant that has become popular in the food industry as a sweetener. The plant comes from the dandelion family and is primarily used as a coffee substitute. The root is where you’re going to find the inulin used in sweeteners. You can also eat the leaves of a chicory root. There are many health benefits to incorporating chicory root as an inulin sweetener into your diet. 
Health Benefits of Inulin 
Improves Digestion 
We are all about gut health and improving digestion as much as we can. Inulin is known to regulate the microbiome. Since it’s a soluble fiber, when inulin gets into your gut and meets water, it becomes a gel. This gel slowly works its way through your body and slows down digestion as well as feeds the good bacteria in your gut along the way.
Relieves Constipation 
You already know being constipated is no fun. Inulin sweeteners may help with constipation by promoting regularity. Again, since it’s dietary fiber, it will stimulate the bowels and get everything going down there. 
May Help With Weightloss 
Consuming inulin sweetener may help with weight loss. Not only are you reducing your sugar intake, but you’re increasing your fiber intake. You’ll feel full longer, and inulin may help curb unwanted snacking habits.

Inulin Sweetener May Help With Other Health Concerns 
If you’re dealing with gastrointestinal problems or Type 2 diabetes, inulin may be able to help. Inulin can help to repair the gut microbiome and stabilize your blood sugar levels. 
Inulin as a Sweetener 
If you’re interested in using inulin as a sweetener, there are several ways to do so. Inulin has been used in processed foods because it is so adaptable. Inulin can not only be added as a sugar substitute, but it can help with texture in foods to replace other things as well. When looking for inulin sweetener, it could have different names such as:  


 Inulin


 Inulin Powder 


 Chicory Root Fiber 


 Chicory Root Inulin


 Native Chicory Inulin 

Basically, if you’re looking for inulin, anything with chicory root in it will be good.  There are so many ways to use inulin sweetener since it comes in a powder form. For example, inulin sweetener can be used as a flour replacement in baked goods without losing any texture elements. Inulin contains 25-35% of the food energy of carbohydrates, as well. So, when you use inulin sweetener you’re getting a lot more than you would with regular old sugar. 
Ways to Use Inulin Sweetener 
Add it to Your Morning Coffee 
Inulin is water-soluble, so it will dissolve in hot drinks without clumping or anything weird happening. You can feel good about adding fiber to your daily cup of coffee or tea.

Throw it in a Smoothie  
We love smoothies, and you probably do too. Smoothies are a great way to get your supplements in for the day. Throw a scoop of inulin powder into your smoothie to get the day going.
Bake With Inulin
Inulin is a sweetener, so it makes perfect sense that you can use it when you bake! Try replacing sugar or whatever sweetener you’re using when you bake with inulin. This is a fabulous way to break a nasty sugar habit. Yes, inulin may not be a powerful sweetener like sugar, but you’ll get used to it. You will probably enjoy it more when you realize how much better you feel. 
Glaze a Ham 
If you’re cooking meat, you can use inulin in a glaze instead of real sugar. You will still get plenty of texture, and fiber too! Not a meat-eater? Try glazing carrots with inulin to make a sweet and healthy side dish. 
Try it in a Cold Drink
One of the drawbacks to sugar is that it doesn’t dissolve in cold drinks. With inulin, you can add it to your favorite iced beverage with no issues. If you have a hard time remembering to throw it in, try a drink that comes with inulin sweetener. We suggest Half Day Tea Tonics. Drinking tea with prebiotics and fiber already in it will make you feel good about your afternoon ‘pick me up’. 

 
Put it on Your Fruit 
Do you ever sprinkle your fruit with sugar? Try inulin sweetener instead. This is a really easy way to add a healthy punch to your snack.  
Why Should You Replace Sugar with Inulin Sweetener?
It can be hard to say goodbye to sugar and replace it with an inulin sweetener. Trust us, your body will thank you for your sacrifice. If you’re having gut problems, sugar could be the culprit. Sugar is linked to problems such as leaky gut syndrome, and the only way to help resolve the issue is to kick the sugar. 
We spend most of our days so busy that we don’t think twice about what we put in our bodies. Doing what we can to reduce the number of processed foods we ingest can do wonders for our gut health and general well-being. 
Conclusion
To sum it up, inulin sweetener is a great alternative to sugar and other artificial sweeteners. It’s found naturally in chicory root and other plants. Inulin sweetener is also an excellent source of dietary fiber, so you can feel good about making the switch.  
If you want to start adding inulin sweetener to your diet, try using products that already contain it first. Half Day Tea Tonics is a great place to start on your inulin sweetener journey.

Is Arizona Green Tea Good For You? Spoiler Alert: The Answer is No
 – Halfday Iced Tea
pages.description: It tastes great, but the nutrition label isn't your best friend. Learn more about what's in an Arizona Iced Tea and alternatives that give you the same taste without the sugar.

headings.text: Is Arizona Green Tea Good For You? Spoiler Alert: The Answer is No
Sugar Content in AriZona Iced Tea
Alternatives to AriZona Green Tea With Ginseng

structured_data.articleBody:
We’ve all seen the aesthetically pleasing cans filled with pretty colors and promises of healthy ingredients. They’re literally everywhere. You can’t go to a gas station without a row of Arizona iced tea catching your eye. If you’re looking for something that’s supposed to be healthy at a great price point of $.99 cents, why wouldn’t you grab one?
Green tea is notoriously healthy, and the Arizona green tea can boasts not only delicious tea but ingredients like honey and ginseng. They do a fantastic job of making a healthy looking product that’s at a great price point. Yes, it does taste good, but at what cost? For an affordable price like they advertise, it’s too good to be true, right? Yes, it is. Arizona iced tea comes in many flavors, and they’re all jam-packed with enough sugar to outweigh any health benefits you may be getting.  
Tea is a great addition to any diet, and it can help you resolve gut health issues. With antioxidants and other healing properties, you can and should be drinking tea. Is Arizona green tea healthy? Probably not. Let’s look at Arizona green tea nutrition facts, and what you can drink instead. 
Arizona Green Tea Nutrition Facts 
To start, let’s break down what’s really going on inside those lovely teal cans. At first glance, this product lures you in with words like ‘ginseng’ and ‘honey.’ Seeing these health-conscious buzzwords on the can make it easy to forget to read the fine print.  
One of the most important things you should do when buying products like this is to check the label for nutrition facts. Arizona iced tea is commonly sold in 23oz cans, and it’s easy to suck the whole sugary concoction down in minutes. If you look at the fine print, one serving is 8oz. So, that means each can is around 3 servings! 
Ginseng 
When you see the word ginseng, your mind automatically assumes healthy. That’s because it is! Ginseng is a Chinese herb that has been used for medicinal purposes for centuries. When it’s used properly, ginseng can boost your immunity, enhance memory and give you more energy. Studies have shown that ginseng’s therapeutic properties may be helpful in treating:  


 Alzheimer’s 


 Parkinson’s Disease


 Depression


 And more 

The seemingly endless health benefits of ginseng are why Arizona Iced Tea was quick to slap it on the label. In 2019, AriZona was sued in a class-action lawsuit stating that AriZona green tea did not actually have ginseng extract in it’s ingredients. While there may be small amounts of ginseng extract present in AriZona green tea, the sheer amount of sugar listed in the nutrition facts is enough to cancel it out. 
Sugar Content in AriZona Iced Tea 
The American Heart Association recommends limiting added sugars to no more than 6 percent of your daily calories. That’s about 9 teaspoons a day for men, and 6 for women. AiZona iced tea greatly exceeds these limits in just one can, and this is why paying attention to the nutrition facts is so important.
One can of AriZona green tea is 23oz, and a single serving is listed at 8oz. The nutrition facts for AriZona green tea list 17g of sugar for each serving. That’s a lot of sugar! Other teas they sell such as AriZona sweet tea have 21g per serving, and AriZona peach tea has 17g per serving, as well. So, if you at a 23oz can of AriZona iced tea, most will have around 68g. You certainly aren’t going to save part of your $.99 cent can for later, people tend to finish them in one sitting. 
The sugar content in AriZona iced tea comes from high fructose corn syrup, as well. We all know this type of sweetener is not great, but we’ll explain why. You can find this type of sweetener in almost every mass-produced drink like sodas and juice. It’s cheap and easy to get from suppliers, which makes it a popular choice for companies. The problem is that in liquid form, your body will absorb the sugar faster in the gut, which can cause an increase in fat. 
Normal sugar contains glucose, which will be broken down into the bloodstream, but fructose goes to your liver. This can cause health problems like fatty liver disease, diabetes and hut health issues. High fructose corn syrup can even decrease the diversity of bacteria in your gut microbiome. So, if you’re trying to improve your gut health AriZona iced tea, and anything with high fructose corn syrup should be avoided. Do not be fooled by the labels on AriZona ice tea, and always read the nutrition facts! 
AriZona does offer a diet green tea, which contains only 1g of sugar per serving. This is still an artificial sweetener, however.  The drinks are marketed as better alternatives to soda, but they appear to iclude similar ingredients. 
AriZona Hard Iced Tea 
A recent item that the AriZona tea company has rolled out is their alcohol beverages. AriZona hard iced tea looks just like the regular cans, advertising the same healthy ingredients along with alochol. It could be easy to miss that it’s alcoholic looking at that label, too. Even though it’s alcoholic, it has tea so it’s going to be easier on your gut, right? Wrong. 
Regardless of being mixed with AriZona tea, alcohol is famously bad for gut health. Your microbiome, which is home to an ecosystem of over 50 trillion bacteria is a special place. Drinking alcohol can kill off the good bacteria, causing an imbalance in your gut. Alcohol can also lead to overgrowth of badb acteria which can cause bloating, indigestion and other problems in the gut. Is Brisk Lemon Iced Tea actually tea?

structured_data.articleBody:
Teas are one of the healthiest beverages on the planet. A nice hot cup in the morning is loaded with antioxidants and various natural substances that are beneficial for our health. If you'd prefer a deliciously refreshing drink instead, iced tea is a great alternative that you can make at home. Simply brew your favorite tea, allow it to steep, pour it into a container full of ice, add a squirt of lemon, and enjoy. 
With iced tea sharing the spotlight as one of the healthiest drinks around, it's no wonder that major beverage companies have taken note. One such company is Lipton, which offers a line of canned and bottled flavored iced teas under the Brisk Iced Tea umbrella. Sounds like the perfect mix of healthy and convenient, right? Wrong. It claims to be iced tea, but the long list of ingredients says otherwise.  
Let's take a look at this popular iced beverage to answer this question: Is Brisk Iced Tea healthy?
What is Brisk Iced Tea?
Brisk Iced Tea is a line of iced tea beverages made by the Lipton company. It's available in several flavors, including the popular Lemon, Raspberry, Sweet Tea, and Half & Half (Lemonade and Iced Tea). 
After their launch in 1991, Brisk Iced Tea quickly became one of the most popular iced tea brands in the United States. This was largely due to their high-profile campaigns that featured celebrities like Eminem, Sylvester Stalone, Danny DeVito, Ozzy Osbourne, Bruce Willis, and so many more.
Despite its popularity, Brisk Iced Teas did face some backlash for the whopping 44 grams of sugar (11 teaspoons) that were added to every 16oz can. They were forced to reformulate, reducing the sugar content by about half using sucralose, one of the many questionable substances on their lengthy list of ingredients.
Understanding that lengthy list of ingredients
If you take a look at the ingredients list for Brisk Lemon Iced Tea, you might be surprised to see that there are 12 total ingredients. For something that is supposed to be iced tea, which traditionally consists of 3-4 ingredients (water, tea, lemon, and an optional sweetener), that's a lot of extras. 
Out of those 12 ingredients, black tea powder, water, and natural flavors are the only ones you'd find in your traditional glass of iced tea. The other 9 are a mix of chemicals, artificial sweeteners, and preservatives.
Let's break them down: the first ingredient is water, followed by high fructose corn syrup (HFCS), citric acid, and a long list of other chemicals. Many of these additives, which we'll explain in further detail below, are synthetic substances that have been linked to health concerns like heart disease, obesity, and more. 
High fructose corn syrup: This is a sweetener made from cornstarch that is found in many processed foods. It's been linked to obesity, heart disease, and various other health concerns.
Citric acid: This is a preservative and flavor enhancer that is often made from GMO citrus fruits. While safe in small doses, excessive amounts can erode the enamel on your teeth.
Sodium polyphosphates: These chemicals are added to processed foods as preservatives. It is generally considered safe by the FDA but should be avoided by people with kidney problems. 
Phosphoric acid: This is another preservative that is often used in processed foods to extend the shelf life and preserve the sharpness of the flavor. Consuming too much phosphate can cause bone, heart, and kidney problems and further aggravate existing kidney conditions. 
Sodium benzoate: Another preservative used to inhibit mold and bacteria growth in food. While considered safe by the FDA, studies have shown an increased risk of obesity, allergies, oxidative stress, and inflammation.
Potassium sorbate: This is yet another preservative. While it is considered safe by the FDA, it has been linked to skin irritation and allergies.
Acesulfame potassium: This artificial sweetener is 200 times sweeter than sugar. One study done using lab animals found that it caused significant shifts in the gut microbiome, leading to weight gain and chronic inflammation. 
Sucralose: An artificial sweetener over 600 times sweeter than sugar. It's often used as a substitute for sugar in diet foods. While it is generally safe, it can reduce the number of good bacteria in your gut microbiome by half. Commonly reported side effects are headaches, intense stomach cramps, and diarrhea.
Calcium disodium EDTA: This is a food additive used to preserve the color and flavor of processed foods. While it is considered safe, more than 3 grams per day can cause low calcium levels and kidney damage. 
After reviewing this list of ingredients, it’s clear that Brisk Lemon Iced Tea is not the healthy tea beverage we've been led to believe. Out of the 12 total ingredients, 3 of them are sweeteners, and the remaining 6 are some form of preservative.
Is Brisk Lemon Iced Tea actually tea?
At this point, you may be wondering if Brisk Lemon Iced Tea is even tea. Traditional iced tea is made by steeping tea leaves or tea bags in hot water and then pouring it over ice. This process is what gives iced tea its signature flavor and brings out the beneficial antioxidants and polyphenols that make tea so healthful.
Surprisingly, there's actually very little tea in a Brisk Ice Tea. Sitting at number 5 on the ingredients list, the black tea powder imparts very little of its flavor, benefits, and caffeine content to the final product.  
In fact, there are only 11 mg of caffeine in a 12oz can, whereas a 12oz serving of black tea will typically contain at least 70mg. This is largely due to the fact that Brisk's Lemon Iced Tea is made using a very small amount of the processed instant black tea powder that has been stripped of most of its beneficial nutrients.
Is Diet Brisk Iced Tea healthy?
While diet drinks are often marketed as being a healthier alternative, this is typically not the case. When reviewing the nutritional facts and ingredients in Brisk's Diet Lemon Iced Tea, all of the harmful preservatives remain, while the only difference is that high fructose corn syrup and sucralose have been replaced by Aspartame. 
Aspartame is among the most controversial artificial sweeteners on the market. Dozens of studies and years of research have linked Aspartame to some severe health problems, including: 


 Strokes


 Seizures


 Heart disease


 Cancer


 Alzheimer's and Dementia


A healthy alternative to Brisk Iced Tea
If you're wondering how to get the grab-and-go convenience of Brisk without the terrifying list of questionable ingredients, try a Halfday. Our delicious tea tonics are excellent for your gut, low in sugar (4g or lower), and have the same classic iced tea taste that you love without any of the junk. Additionally, all of our teas are made with real tea extracts, natural flavors, and organic ingredients you can trust. 

Here at Halfday, we believe that you shouldn't have to sacrifice great taste in exchange for healthy options which is why our tea tonics are the perfect alternative to sugary and processed iced teas like Brisk.  
So next time you're feeling thirsty, reach for a Halfday and enjoy the great taste of iced tea without the junk!

Brisk Iced Tea is a line of iced tea beverages made by the Lipton company. What Kind of Tea is in Snapple Peach Tea?

structured_data.articleBody:
Tea is one of the most popular beverages on the planet, so it’s no surprise that there’s an almost endless list of brands on the market. One such brand is Snapple, which can be found at pretty much any retailer in the United States.
Those adorable and delicious Snapple bottles can be irresistible. The sweet, refreshing taste and nostalgia keep you coming back. It says ‘all-natural’ on the label, so that means it’s healthy, right? Well, not really. 
Popular drinks like Peach Snapple are advertised as healthy, but they are packed with sugar and other components that aren’t great for you. If you’re looking to get rid of bloating and focus on your gut health, it’s best to stay away from products like Snapple. 
The Snapple Peach Tea of your youth that you chugged before science class is a bit of a liar. Just because ingredients are considered natural, doesn’t mean they’re good for you or your digestive system. This is why it’s so important to look at the nutrition fact and do your research on a product if you’re trying to improve your gut health. Let’s look at whether Peach Snapple is good for you, and what to drink instead.
What Exactly is Snapple? 
In case you might have spent the 90s under a rock, Snapple is most often known as the classic peach iced tea in the glass bottle we all know and love. Snapple is a brand of tea and juice drinks owned by the Dr. Pepper company. They have a variety of sugary flavors like Snapple Peach Tea that have been popular favorites since the 1970s. Currently, there are 29 different Snapple flavors listed on the website from Snapple Peach Tea to Snapple Apple.  
If you’ve ever wandered through a convenience store, you have seen the glass bottle with blue caps. The labels advertise all-natural teas packed with flavor. The caps also have an interesting fact printed on them, so you’re rewarded with trivia when you open it. Snapple has also recently switched to a more sustainable bottle and went through a visual rebrand. Snapple ditched the glass bottles for recycled plastic.  
While Snapple advertises an all-natural product, it’s important to read the label. These delicious bottled drinks are mostly made of sugar and other ingredients that aren’t great for you, such as aspartame and citric acid that’s also found in household cleaners.    
Read the Fine Print 
Snapple peach tea bottles are not big and sold in drink sections that make them appear to be single servings. They’re not. If you look closely at the label, each 16oz bottle of Snapple is meant to be two servings. Along with the fact that you are drinking double of what you should, Snapple is overloaded with sugar. We already know too much sugar is almost always a bad thing for our health.  
When you go down the list of ingredients on a bottle of Snapple, the second listed ingredient is sugar after water, which means it has a very high amount. More than any other ingredient in the bottle. Each bottle of Snapple contains a whopping 42 grams of sugar! That’s the equivalent of 10.5 teaspoons, which is above the daily average for suggested sugar intake for the ENTIRE DAY. Snapple also contains 160-170 calories in each bottle.  
Another ingredient to look out for is citric acid. Naturally found in citrus fruits, citric acid is what gives them the sour taste you get when you eat them. In Peach Snapple, however, the citric acid listed in the ingredients is manufactured and doesn’t come naturally in fruit. It’s the same thing they use for lemon cleaning products, and you’re drinking it.  
One of the best benefits you can get from drinking tea is the antioxidants. Well, drinks like Snapple contain no antioxidants. By the time it becomes Snapple, it’s barely even tea at that point. Antioxidants are what give tea a bitter taste, so the makers of Snapple water it down so as not to take away from how delicious it is. Tea that is stored for a long time will also lose antioxidants over time, which is what happens to Snapple in the bottle. 
What About Diet Snapple Peach Tea?
Diet Snapple flavors like peach tea advertise all-natural ingredients, which doesn’t always mean better. For example, the flavorings used in drinks, whether natural or not, aren’t great for you. According to Scientific American, artificial flavoring can potentially be safer since it’s manufactured in a controlled environment and undergoes testing.  
Diet versions of Snapple are advertised as healthier with less sugar. Unfortunately, the sugar in Diet Snapple Peach Tea is replaced with aspartame. This artificial sweetener is low in calories, so many diet products on the market contain it. It’s sweeter than sugar and is advertised as a healthy option because it lower’s the amount of actual sugar you’re ingesting. This does not, however, make it good for you or your gut.  
Aspartame is made of two amino acids called aspartic acid and phenylalanine. It’s around 200 times sweeter than natural sugars, but the lower calorie count is what makes it so popular. While it was designed to promote weight loss, research has shown that aspartame usually does the opposite. Not only that, but aspartame has been linked to serious medical conditions such as brain tumors and cancer.  
What Kind of Tea is in Snapple Peach Tea?
There are several types of tea, and each have different health benefits. You might be wondering what type of tea is in Snapple, because they don’t list it in the ingredients. If you dig around online, product descriptions list Snapple Peach Tea as being made from a blend of green and black tea. 
Benefits of Tea 
If you’ve been drinking Snapple Peach Tea for the benefits that come from tea, it’s important to understand that you aren’t getting them. There are, however, many benefits to drinking tea in other forms. Since Snapple tea is made from green and black teas, let’s look at the benefits of drinking these types of teas as peach tea and other alternatives. 
Black Tea 
Black tea is a very common type of tea and comes from the Camellia sinensis plant. It’s commonly blended with spices and flavors to make different blends like chai and Earl Grey. If you like a kick with your tea, black tea has a higher caffeine amount than most other teas.  
In its natural form, black tea is full of antioxidants which we already know have many health benefits. Black tea contains plyphenols, which can help keep your gut bacteria balanced, as well. This type of tea may also help lower cholesterol, and reduce blood pressure.
Green Tea 
Green tea is considered one of the healthiest beverages on the planet. It can be drunk in many ways and is always delicious. Green tea is full of antioxidants as well and is a great way to hydrate.  
Green tea may also improve brain function. This is because of the caffeine content. Green tea, and black tea for that matter are also great alternatives to coffee. If you’ve been trying to cut back on caffeine, switching to tea can give you the caffeine boost without the jitters since there is less in tea.
Alternatives to Snapple Peach Tea 
1. HALFDAY ICED TEA
If you’re ready to move on from sugary drinks like Snapple Peach Tea, there are plenty of alternatives that taste just as great. Halfday has been featured on sights like Weight Watchers as well as found in Target stores nationwide. Here are some of the stats: 

35 calories vs. 160 calories in Peach Snapple 
3g of sugar vs. 40 grams of sugar in Peach Snapple 
8g fiber vs. 0 g fiber in Peach Snapple 
Identical taste! 

2. MAKE YOUR OWN. 

For one, you can make your own tea at home! The internet is full of recipes that can help you replicate Snapple Peach Tea at home without all of the unnecessary ingredients.  Making your own tea at home is a great way to ensure you know exactly what you’re getting. If you’re working on improving gut health, you want to avoid processed ingredients and excess sugar. You can pick up loose leaf tea at most stores and brew it yourself. That way, you know that all that’s in it is tea and water, and whatever else you add.  
 

If you're ready for the easy way to drink your favorite Snapple, try HalfDay Tea Tonics. The Peach Green Tea is a great replacement for the peach Snapple of your past. Unlike Snapple peach tea, Halfday teas are loaded with plant fiber to introduce more prebiotics into your gut. This will help you keep your gut healthy and avoid unnecessary bloating from sugar-loaded drinks. 
Conclusion
The bottom line about Snapple - no it’s not healthy, even if it's delicious. Loaded with sugar and ingredients linked to health problems, it may be time to switch to an alternative. It can be easy to think any product containing tea is going to be good for you, but you’ve got to read the fine print. The best alternative on the market is Halfday iced tea, which is identical in taste with way fewer calories and sugar.  

Diet Snapple Peach Tea and other drinks in the Snapple universe contain ingredients like aspartame. These products have less sugar, but artificial sweeteners can cause other health problems. 
Reading the label is important when buying anything that you’re going to eat or drink. It’s especially important when you’re working to improve gut health. So, put down that Snapple Peach Tea and try a healthier alternative today!

So, put down that Snapple Peach Tea and try a healthier alternative today! Back to blog

pages.description: Coffee was the third most popular drink in 2021. For some, it’s a breakfast essential, and for others, it’s something to warm them up. The latest question being asked is if there is fiber in coffee? And the short answer is yes.

headings.text: How Much Fiber Do You Need? How Much Does Coffee Have?

structured_data.articleBody:
Who doesn’t enjoy a nicely brewed cup of coffee? Even if you aren’t big on cappuccinos, espressos, or lattes, you will probably still want a mocha or an iced coffee. There are various ways in which coffee is brewed and served, and often it’s something that people take very seriously.
65% of all coffee is consumed during the first few hours of the day. For some, brewing coffee is like a morning ritual and something that they pay close attention to and spend a lot of time and money on. Others need a quick coffee in the morning to wake up their mind. All in all, people love and need their coffee.



Overall, there is substantial consumption of coffee around the globe. Between 2020 and 2021, more than 166.63 million 60 kg bags of coffee were consumed worldwide. The most consumption was in Scandinavian countries, where the winters are long and dark. When there is something consumed so frequently, questions about its health benefits are bound to arise.
For years, scientists and researchers have been trying to understand how coffee impacts our bodies. Many pieces of research have been conducted into its effects on heart health, antioxidant properties, and other health benefits and possible negative impacts.
Recently, the question about the presence of fiber in coffee has been raised. While scientists had already stated that coffee beans contain fiber, it has recently been reported that brewed coffee contains fiber too.
So what does it mean if your morning cup of coffee contains fibers, and how does it impact you?
What is fiber?
Dietary fiber is an essential macronutrient required for the normal function of one’s body. It is a type of carbohydrate that is not digested by the body but plays a vital role in maintaining gut health.
Carbohydrates are divided into simple sugars (monosaccharides and disaccharides), complex sugars (polysaccharides), and fiber. Simple sugars include glucose, fructose, sucrose, and these help in providing energy for the body. They are easily absorbed into the bloodstream and cells. Glucose is also the only source of energy for the brain. Complex sugars such as starch are broken down in the body into simple sugars and then absorbed and utilized.
Dietary fiber is divided into two categories; soluble and insoluble fiber. Soluble fiber is the edible part of plants resistant to digestion and absorption in the human small intestine. However, the bacteria in the gut partially or completely ferment it to short-chain fatty acids in the large intestine. These fibers absorb water and form gels which slow down digestion throughout the digestive tract.
Insoluble fibers pass through the digestive tract largely intact and are not broken down or changed via the gut biome or enzymes. 
Why do you need fiber?
Soluble and insoluble fibers have different compositions; hence they have different actions and functions in the body. However, both are involved in adding volume to food without much caloric content and giving a feeling of fullness or satiety without too much calorie consumption. They are also both involved in maintaining normal intestinal pH levels. 
Due to their property of absorbing water and becoming gel-like, soluble fibers slow down stomach emptying and digestion of carbohydrates in the stomach. They also make food move faster through the intestine and reduce glucose absorption. These actions reduce glucose absorption and fewer spikes in blood sugar levels. The lowered appetite and less absorption of glucose also help in weight loss.
Soluble fiber has also been shown to reduce cholesterol and unhealthy lipid (LDL) levels. This means that these fibers reduce the risk of coronary heart disease.
Insoluble fibers, on the other hand, are more involved in adding bulk to stool, facilitating the fast movement of passage through the digestive tract, and reducing the risk of constipation, hemorrhoids, and other gut pathologies. Research has also shown a significant relationship between high fiber intake and a lower incidence rate of colorectal cancers.
How Much Fiber Do You Need? How Much Does Coffee Have? 
The recommended daily intake for dietary fiber is 25 g/day for women and 38 g/day for men. However, the daily intake of individuals in North America is less than 50% of the recommended value, at about 15g/day.
The research was conducted by Fulgencio Saura-Calixto, Ph.D., and colleagues at the Spanish National Research Council in Madrid to measure the amount of dietary fiber in brewed freeze-dried instant coffee, espresso, and filtered coffee.
The results showed that instant coffee contained the most fiber, about 1.8 grams per cup. Espresso contained roughly 1.5g of dietary fiber per cup, and filtered coffee only provided 1.1g of dietary fiber in each cup.
Other studies were later conducted, and they showed that Arabica coffee beans provide more dietary fiber than Robusta beans. It was also revealed that decaf coffee has less dietary fiber than caffeine coffee.



However, the bottom line was that you would have to drink a lot of coffee to get to the recommended daily value of dietary fiber. But, you can drink coffee for its other benefits, such as its antioxidant activity, providing micronutrients like vitamin B2, potassium, magnesium, and reducing the risk of diseases like Parkinson’s disease and type 2 diabetes.
Juices and other beverages with fiber
Freshly squeezed juices are a healthy and delicious way to get your daily fiber. Juices like apple juice, lemon juice, and carrot juice are tasty and healthy beverages that you can have in the morning to keep you healthy and happy. 
Premade beverages like Halfday’s healthy and delicious iced teas are a great source of fiber, and contain over 30% of your daily recommended fiber intake. These teas were formulated specially to maintain gut health. They taste just like sweetened iced tea, and are the real deal to get your fiber in. 
The primary flavors available are a delicious lemon black tea, a nostalgic green tea with honey and ginseng, and a refreshing peach green tea. A limited-edition cranberry black tea flavor is also available. All these flavors are equally delicious and healthy.
 

 
 
Each can is 355 ml and contains 35-40 calories only. The teas are sweet and refreshing but have small amounts of sugar to ensure that you remain healthy. Each can contains 8g of dietary fiber, which means you are getting as much as 22% of the daily recommended value from just a single can.
All flavors are made from natural organic tea and are vegan and paleo-friendly. So if you have such dietary restrictions, these drinks are an excellent option for you when you are craving a refreshing iced tea. So now you can easily enjoy a fun, refreshing drink on the poolside with your friends and stay healthy, happy, and fresh.
Other sources of fiber
As discussed above, coffee is not enough to provide you with your daily requirement for dietary fiber, so you must incorporate other sources of fiber into your meals. The sources of fiber are all plant and grain-based. Supplements are sometimes prescribed to patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
For insoluble fiber, whole-grain foods, nuts, and legumes are great dietary additions. You can also incorporate vegetables like green beans, celery, courgettes, and cauliflower into your daily meals. Another simple thing that can increase your insoluble fiber uptake is leaving the skins of potatoes and tomatoes on in your meals and eating them. The skin of many fruits and vegetables is high in insoluble fibers.



For soluble fiber, legumes, oats, chia seeds, and rye are excellent sources. Nuts, especially almonds, also contain a substantial amount of soluble fiber. Root vegetables such as sweet potatoes and onions are also excellent sources and are easy to incorporate into your diet.
Bottom Line
Coffee is a great breakfast drink which is why it is enjoyed by so many around the globe. It also has a range of health benefits and gives consumers a sense of euphoria and happiness right after consumption. However, when it comes to fiber content, you are better off consuming other drinks such as Halfday’s Iced Teas or natural juices. It is also essential that you understand that one product alone is not enough to provide you with your daily requirements. You must incorporate multiple sources to ensure that you remain healthy and fit.

pages.description: You've seen and heard of it everywhere. But what does Kombucha taste like exactly? Learn more and tips and tricks on what it is and how to make your own!

headings.text: Kombucha 101: What Does Kombucha Taste Like?
What Are The Benefits Of Kombucha?
How To Make Your Own Kombucha
Top 4 Mistakes Made When Brewing Your Own Kombucha
Not letting it ferment long enough
Using The Wrong Container To Brew Your Kombucha

structured_data.articleBody:
Kombucha tea is very popular in the United States, and if you've noticed, it's started to become prevalent on local restaurant drink lists and has started to fill the aisles of grocery stores. However, if you've been hearing a ton about the beverage but are still wondering, "what does Kombucha taste like?" you're not alone. In this blog post, we will discuss what Kombucha is, what it tastes like, and how to make your own at home.
What Is Kombucha?
Kombucha is a fermented tea that has been around for centuries. It's made by adding a SCOBY (symbiotic colony of bacteria and yeast) to sweetened black or green tea. This mixture is then left to ferment for anywhere from one to four weeks. The result is a slightly sweet, slightly vinegary, somewhat carbonated beverage that is rich in probiotics and refreshing to enjoy.
What Does Kombucha Taste Like?
Kombucha has a unique, somewhat harsher flavor that is often described as tangy, sweet, and slightly effervescent. Some people compare the taste to sparkling apple cider or white wine. The longer the kombucha ferments, the more vinegary it will taste. You can also experiment with different types of tea, sweeteners, and fruits to create your own unique flavor combination. This means that there are essentially hundreds of different flavor combinations that you can try.
If the carbonated, stronger flavor profile of Kombucha isn't your favorite, no stress at all. There are plenty of other good-for-your-gut drinks on the market. Halfday Iced Tea tastes just like Snapple, Arizona Iced Tea, and your other long-time favorites, but better for you with plenty of health benefits. Each can is loaded up with 30% of your daily fiber and probiotics! 
 

What Are The Benefits Of Kombucha?
Besides being a delicious tasting beverage, there are many reasons that people choose to drink Kombucha over alternative drinks like soda or juice. This includes benefits such as: 
Great Source Of Probiotics
One of the most significant sources of probiotics is fermented foods like Kombucha. Probiotics are beneficial bacteria that help keep your gut healthy and improve digestion. Kombucha is a great way to get your daily dose of probiotics and support gut health because it contains live and active cultures that are released during the fermentation process. 
During this process, multiple acidic compounds and acids combine together to form what is known as glucuronic acid. This compound has been shown to possess detoxifying effects, making Kombucha an excellent drink for people who are looking to cleanse their system. 
Support Immune System
Kombucha is also rich in antioxidants, which are known to help boost the immune system. Antioxidants help protect your cells from damage and can reduce inflammation. This makes Kombucha a great drink to have on hand when you're feeling under the weather or want to prevent getting sick.
Healthy Beverage To Drink
Unlike soda or other sugary drinks, Kombucha is a healthy alternative that you can feel good about drinking. It's low in calories, sugar, and caffeine and contains no artificial flavors or colors. Kombucha is also vegan-friendly and gluten-free, making it an excellent option for people with dietary restrictions. In addition, this beverage is the perfect way to hydrate and fuel your body.
Increased Energy Level
Many people who drink kombucha report feeling more energized after drinking it. This is likely due to the probiotics and antioxidants that are working together to support optimal health. So if you're looking for a drink that will give you an added boost, Kombucha is a great option.
How To Make Your Own Kombucha
If you're interested in giving Kombucha a try, you can easily make your own at home. All you need is a few simple ingredients and a SCOBY. You can find all of these items online or at your local health food store or create them from scratch. The general process includes the following steps:
Make Your SCOBY
The SCOBY or symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast is referred to as the "mother" because it is used to make future batches of Kombucha. It helps to protect your tea from harmful contaminants, ferment the tea you're making, and add good bacteria into the batch.
The ingredients you'll need to make your own include 1/2 cup of sugar, 1 cup unflavored Kombucha, four bags of black tea, rubber bands, cheesecloth, and a large glass container.

Start by boiling the water in a clean pot.
Next, remove the pot from heat and add the sugar into the water. At the same time, allow the tea to steep until the entire mixture cools down.
Next, pour the tea into your glass jars and add store-bought Kombucha into each one.
Once divided up, cover the top with cheesecloth and secure with a rubber band.

You'll need to place it in a room-temperature space that's dark for 1 to 4 weeks. You'll know it's ready once it forms a 1/4 inch SCOBY at the top. 
Create The First Fermentation
Once you've formed the SCOBY, you can then actually make the Kombucha. To do this, you're going to boil 14 cups of water and then remove from the heat and add the sugar, allowing it to dissolve. Next, you'll add 8-10 bags of black tea, allowing it to steep and cool until it reaches room temperature.
Next, you'll separate the mixture into jars and add the SCOBY on top. Cover it with a few layers of cheesecloth and secure with rubber bands. Again, let it sit in a room temperature, dark room for 6 to 10 days. Begin tasting the tea at 5 days to see how it tastes.
Second Fermentation Process
Once your first fermentation has finished, you'll strain out the floaties and remove the SCOBY from your tea. Next, the fermented tea should be placed into bottles with some type of sweetener (honey or sugar is great) and again sealed with a lid.
