structured_data.articleBody:
If you’ve ever strolled down the drink aisle at Whole Foods, you’ve seen the vast selection of kombucha. Trying something new can be daunting, but trust us when we say kombucha is worth it. This fizzy beverage is a great way to give yourself an energy boost during the day while being kind to your gut. 
While kombucha is advertised as a healthy drink, there is still little research on the benefits. This drink is, however, packed with vitamins and other compounds that have known health benefits in other foods. Kombucha is said to promote gut health, boost immunity, and could potentially help combat serious health conditions like cancer. This fermented drink can be a bit of an acquired taste, and knowing what it’s made will probably make you feel better about trying it out. 
Kombucha has been used by humans for centuries, and adding it to your diet can help you improve gut health. So, let’s look at what it is, the benefits, and the best time to drink kombucha. 
What is Kombucha?
To start, kombucha is a fizzy fermented drink that’s made of tea, sugar, bacteria, and yeast. If it sounds scary, it isn’t. You probably eat and drink plenty of fermented things without realizing it! Kombucha is often referred to as a functional beverage because it contains vitamins, amino acids, and other nutrients that can provide us with health benefits. 
There’s no concrete invention date, but kombucha is thought to have been invented in China or Japan around 220 B.C. It’s sometimes referred to as mushroom tea, but it’s definitely not made out of mushrooms. The main ingredients in kombucha are yeast and bacteria that work together to create a colony that can work together for gut-friendly benefits. 
Some Kombucha studies claim that it can help with serious medical conditions such as blood pressure and cancer. It’s also rich in antibiotics and vitamins, which can provide health benefits such as killing off harmful bacteria in the gut. 
The double-fermentation process creates a fizzy drink that eliminates the alcohol content created by fermentation. You can even make kombucha at home. 
How is Kombucha Made?
To put it simply, kombucha is made by adding bacteria, yeast, and sugar to tea. After about a month of fermentation, you’re left with a drinkable beverage with natural carbonation. The process is fairly simple, and many people practice homebrewing techniques to see what they can come up with. T
What is Fermentation? 
While you may consume fermented foods for gut health, you probably haven’t thought about the process. Fermentation is a process in which molecules like glucose are broken down into a simpler form. It’s typically used to make alcoholic drinks like beer and wine. Since fermentation of pretty much anything will make alcohol, there were some problems with alcohol regulation with kombucha. The kombucha process involves double fermentation, which will stop the production of too much alcohol in the beverage. 
Making Kombucha 
Kombucha starts with a mixture called a SCOBY. A SCOBY is a pancake-shaped blob type thing that kick starts the fermentation process. It’s a culture of bacteria and yeast. When making kombucha, the SCOBY is added to black or green tea. Typically, the tea is sweetened beforehand with a natural sweetener. 
Once everything is mixed together, the baby kombucha should be left at room temperature with a loose cover such as fabric over it to begin the fermentation process. Have you ever forgotten about a container of apple juice in the fridge for months? Congratulations, you fermented something without even realizing it! Don’t drink it though. You’ll catch a buzz, but you will most likely get sick. 
After 1-3 weeks, the mixture should be bottled. When it’s bottled, the CO2 released is kept inside with the liquid which then created carbonation. The kombucha should be stored in the bottle for 1-2 weeks at room temperature for maximum carbonation.  
Then, the kombucha should be refrigerated to slow down the fermentation and carbonation processes. This will make the kombucha drinkable, and keep it at a lower alcohol content. You can even do this on a small scale at home to try making your own! 
Benefits of Kombucha 
When looking at the benefits of Kombucha, it’s important to understand that there is not a lot of research on the subject. Evidence-based research does support and suggests that these benefits can come from drinking this fizzy drink.  
Kombucha Could be a Source of Probiotics 
Probiotics are the good bacteria that live in your digestive system and are crucial to maintaining a healthy gut. Fermented foods such as sauerkraut are excellent sources of probiotics, and kombucha is created through the same process. 
There is no concrete evidence that kombucha does contain large amounts of probiotics, but it does contain lactic-acid bacteria. Lactic acid bacteria are probiotic organisms found in the body and are typically found in fermented dairy products. So, finding them in kombucha could mean it’s a good source of probiotics.
It May Give a Boost to Your Immune System 
We’re always looking for the nest best way to give our immune system a little boost. Fermented foods are known to benefit the immune system, and since kombucha is made the same way, there’s potential for it to do the same thing. Since kombucha is full of antioxidants, it doesn’t hurt to add it to your diet for potential immune system benefits. 
Kombucha Could Increase Your Energy 
The components of kombucha have been proven you increase energy. Since kombucha is typically made with green or black tea, you will also receive a kick from the caffeine. This makes it a good pick-me-up that will be nice to your gut, too. 
Kombucha Contains Vitamins
Studies have shown that kombucha does in fact contain small amounts of vitamins and minerals. Some vitamins in kombucha are vitamin C, B1, and B12. Adding vitamins to your diet is never a bad thing, so it wouldn’t hurt to try kombucha. 
When is The Best Time to Drink Kombucha?
If you’re ready to incorporate kombucha into your diet, you’re probably wondering when the best time of day to drink it is. If you’ve never had it before, it’s important to do your research and take it slow to start. While kombucha can be great for your health, it could also have some health risks. This is especially important if you decide to brew your own at home.  
For the beginner, it’s recommended to start with around 3oz and see how it goes. Once you get a feel for how it affects you, you can increase to more. The last thing you want to happen is to realize it doesn’t agree with you and you’ve already drank a lot of it. 
As for the best time to drink kombucha, you can drink it pretty much whenever you’d like. Since kombucha is tea-based, it contains caffeine and can be a good way to get the day going. Some research shows that drinking kombucha on an empty stomach will help you get the gut health benefits from it, as well. So, if you’re dealing with a bacteria imbalance in your gut, try some booch in the morning! 
Another great time to drink kombucha is in the afternoon after lunch. It’s common to feel a little sluggish in the afternoon, so drinking a fizzy caffeinated drink should do the trick. You can also drink kombucha before lunch to ease your stomach, as well. The fizzy and fermented nature of kombucha also makes it a great alternative to alcohol, so you can try it as a replacement for happy hour or a nightcap! 
If you enjoy kombucha and the probiotic benefits, you’re going to need something with prebiotics to feed that good bacteria. Probiotics are the good bacteria in your gut, and in order to keep you healthy and energized, they need to be healthy and energized too. Maintaining a good amount of plant fiber in your diet will bring in prebiotics, which is a source of food for probiotics. Try Halfday Tea Tonics which are packed with prebiotics to keep your gut balanced and the new bacteria full of energy!
 

Conclusion
The bottom line is that kombucha is a great solution to gut health issues. If you want to know what the best time of day to drink kombucha is, you can drink it whenever you see fit. Keep in mind that it does contain caffeine, so in the morning or afternoon may be better if you’re sensitive to it. 
This fizzy drink is made through the same fermentation process as beer and wine, so it becomes naturally carbonated. If carbonation bothers your stomach, consider adding a prebiotic drink like Haldfay Tea Tonics to your diet to balance out the kombucha. Prebiotics will also keep the new probiotics energized and ready to protect your gut! 
Kombucha is also a great alcohol replacement for a healthy gut lifestyle. Try swapping your nightly cocktail for a glass of kombucha and see how you feel. There are many flavors of kombucha out there, so you’ll be sure to find something just right for you.

headings.text: Natural Herbs to Curb Sugar Cravings and Keep Your Gut in Check
The Problem With Eating Too Much Sugar
What Happens When You Stop Eating Sugar?
It’ll Be Great For Your Teeth
Natural Herbs to Stop Sugar Cravings

structured_data.articleBody:
Everyone loves sugar, but it’s notoriously bad for you for a number of reasons. It’s easy to sit down with a bag of sugary snacks and throw caution to the wind, but trust us, you’ll feel it later. That’s why it’s good to use natural herbs to stop sugar cravings when you can. The problem is that there is sugar in almost everything, and Americans are eating a lot of it. 

In fact, the average American eats about 6 cups of sugar a week, which comes to around 152 pounds of sugar a year. That’s a pretty scary amount when you think about it like that. Not only can sugar cause well-known issues like cavities and weight gain, but it can also wreak havoc on your hormones, sleep, and other parts of the body.
Sugar is a delicious and addictive substance that can be lurking in almost everything we drink or eat. Let’s take a look at why it’s not great to eat a lot of sugar and how you can use natural herbs to stop sugar cravings. 
Why Do We Crave Sugar?
To start, we need to look at why we crave sugar. Sugar is super addictive and can become a problem real quick. It’s a sweet substance that’s found in plans such as sugar cane and harvested to be used in foods to make them sweet. While it may seem innocent enough, sugar can actually have similar effects on the brain to addictive drugs.  
When we are eating something that’s high in sugar content, our brains release serotonin. Your body associates eating sugar with that good feeling you get. The body will also release beta-endorphins when you eat sugar that can act as a natural painkiller. Simply put, when you eat sugar your body feels amazing. That’s why they call it a sugar rush! 
Unfortunately, that feeling you get after eating an entire bag of peanut butter cups is temporary. When you start to feel the negative effects, your body will crave more sugar to get the food feeling back. It’s an unpleasant cycle, and that’s why you should use natural herbs to stop sugar cravings.  
Consuming large amounts of sugar can have long-term negative effects on the mind and body. Not to mention, eating a lot of sugar is horrible for your gut. Eating too much sugar can lead to problems like a leaky gut and increased bad bacteria in the digestive tract.  
Small amounts of sugar are alright, but it’s when you start eating it every day in large quantities that are a problem. The American Heart Association recommends a sugar limit of no more than 100 calories per day. This equates to about 24g of sugar for women and 36g of sugar for men. This number can differ depending on your health and body. If you have concerns, always consult with your doctor. 
The Problem With Eating Too Much Sugar 
Overdoing the sugar will not only make you feel not great, but it can also lead to health complications. Too much sugar may lead to: 


 Heart Disease


 Obesity


 Cavities and Tooth Decay 


 Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease 


 Type-2 Diabetes 


 Hormonal Imbalance 


 Depression 


What Happens When You Stop Eating Sugar?
When you use natural herbs to stop sugar cravings, you’re going to notice a change in your body. This is especially true if you’ve been eating a lot of sugar for a long period of time. It’s important to remember that since sugar is highly addictive, you can experience withdrawal symptoms. It’s not recommended to stop cold turkey, and a little sugar is still going to be alright. If you are dealing with extreme effects from eating a lot of sugar, please consult with your doctor before trying natural herbs to stop your sugar cravings.  
The positive benefits of cutting back on sugar are going to outweigh the uncomfortable adjustment period. So, before you start using natural herbs to stop sugar cravings let’s see what happens to your body. 
Increased Mental Cognition
Reducing your sugar intake is a great way to improve memory and cognition. Have you ever felt foggy-brained after eating a lot of sweets? Studies have shown that diets high in sugar can cause negative changes in the brain. You’ll feel sluggish and be unable to focus. When you stop eating so much sugar, you should notice that you’re more mentally sharp. 
You’ll Lose Weight 
Sugar is notorious for causing weight gain. Sugar is a source of empty calories, so when you eat those midnight cookies you could be adding on the pounds. It’s important to note that it isn’t just the sugar causing the weight gain, it’s how the sugar impacts your body. For example, eating sugar can cause imbalances in the hormones that help you maintain your weight.  
It’ll Be Great For Your Teeth 
We’ve all had the fact that sugar rots your teeth pounding into oour brains since we were little. It is still true! Sugar is directly linked to tooth decay and cavities. Even after you kick the sugar.you should be brushing and flossing twice a day to keep those pearly whites looking and feeling fresh. 
Your Sleep Will Improve 
Have you ever gone ham on a bag of candy before bed and not been able to fall asleep? The hormonal imbalances sugar cause can also hinder your ability to fall asleep, and the sleep you’re getting won’t be the best quality. Before reaching for that midnight cookie, remember that. 
Your Skin Will Thank You 
If you deal with acne and blemishes on a regular basis, sugar could be to blame. Using natural herbs to stop sugar cravings can help you improve your skin. Studies have shown that consuming large amounts of sugar is linked to acne and other ski conditions. Cutting back on sugar will give you a natural glow. 
Natural Herbs to Stop Sugar Cravings 
Now that we know how much you’ll benefit from cutting back on sugar, let’s talk about how to deal with the cravings. Using natural herbs is a great way to stop sugar cravings in their tracks, and you’ll receive other health benefits as well. 
Cinnamon
Who doesn’t love cinnamons? While it’s typically associated with the holidays, cinnamon is a naturally sweet spice that’s loaded with antioxidants. It also has anti-inflammatory properties that are great for the gut. Studies have shown that the polyphenols in cinnamon control your blood glucose levels, which can help reduce sugar cravings. If you like tea, adding cinnamon powder on top is a great way to incorporate it into your daily routine. 
Clove 
Another holiday classic, clove is a natural herb with many health benefits along with helping you stop sugar cravings. When you have an upset stomach, clove is also a great home remedy. It’s full of antioxidants and other compounds that make it anti-inflammatory. Clove is a great addition to tea, or you can cook it into your favorite meals to get the benefits.
Ginseng 
Ginseng is one of the most popular natural herbs in the world, and it can also help stop sugar cravings. It’s an adaptogenic root that may boost your immune system, relieve stress, and improve mental health and well-being.  
Ginseng is also great for blood sugar stabilization, so it’s the perfect natural herb to stop sugar cravings. Research shows that ginseng can lower blood sugar levels in people with type-2 diabetes. 
If you’re looking for a way to get ginseng into your diet, try Halfday’s Green Tea with Honey Ginseng. Not only is it a great way to get ginseng into your diet, but this tea tonic is also full of plant fiber that gives you prebiotics to feed the good bacteria in your gut. It also only has 3g of sugar which is way less than most commercial tea products that contain ginseng on the market.  

Rosemary
When you cut out or lower your sugar intake, one of the side effects can be a headache you can’t shake. Rosemary is a known natural remedy for headaches, so when you’re working on kicking your sugar habit try cooking with rosemary to combat the headaches. There are a lot of recipes that contain rosemary, or you can experiment with adding it to your favorites.   
Turmeric
Turmeric is so hot right now. Everybody is taking it. This natural herb is typically used to help with joint inflammation but has been shown to help aid with blood sugar control. You can take turmeric supplements, or cook with it as a spice to make tasty meals to get it into your diet  

Fenugreek  

Probably a lesser-known natural herb to stop sugar cravings is fenugreek. This herb is harvested in India, the Mediterranean, and North Africa. Studies have shown that fenugreek improves insulin levels in people with diabetes if they take 1 gram a day. 
Conclusion
To sum it up, using natural herbs to stop sugar cravings is a great way to cut back. You don’t have to totally eliminate sugar from your diet, but lowering your intake will give you a number of health benefits. Try cooking with these herbs or taking supplements to get started!

pages.description: Prebiotics and Probiotics are all the rage right now. What exactly is the difference and how can you incorporate them into your life?

headings.text: Prebiotics and Probiotics: What's the Difference?
Common Conditions Probiotics Have Been Known to Help:
Food and Drinks that Contain Prebiotics Naturally

structured_data.articleBody:
Prebiotics and Probiotics are everywhere right now. Health drinks, gut health books, and fitness gurus all speak to the importance of having both in your body. But what exactly is the difference between prebiotics and probiotics? 
To start off, both involve bacteria. Bacteria are typically viewed as a tiny little villain lurking on countertops waiting to make us sick. They aren’t always evil! In fact, our bodies depend on certain types of bacteria to keep us healthy. Gut health is dependent on a balance of good bacteria to avoid bloating, gas and keep your microbiome in order. 
The microbiome consists of the trillions of microorganisms that reside in your gut, such as fungi, parasites, and bacteria. Yes, it sounds scary as these things are all considered bad outside the body, but when they work together they create a healthy digestive system. Every person’s microbiome is unique, and it’s important to keep it balanced. One of the best things you can do for your microbiome is kept the good bacteria healthy.
The good bacteria living in your gut are called probiotics. There are trillions of bacteria lurking in your digestive system working night and day to ensure you stay healthy. Working hard all the time means they will need energy, and they feed off of a substrate called prebiotics. With such similar names, it can be easy to confuse the two. All it takes is one misplaced vowel, and you’re searching for the wrong thing! 
What’s the difference between prebiotics and probiotics, anyway? Let's look at the main differences, and how prebiotics and probiotics work together to maintain gut health and keep the bloat away.
The Importance of Gut Flora
Before diving into the question of what the differences between prebiotics and probiotics are, we need to look at gut flora. Gut flora is the ecosystem found in your digestive tract, and it’s filled with trillions of microorganisms working to keep things moving. In fact, there are twice as many microbes living in your gut as cells in your entire body. That’s a lot! 
Your gut flora is so important to your health. It regulates your immune system and aids in digestion. If you’ve ever dealt with gas and bloating, there was probably an imbalance in your gut flora from something you ate. The good news is it can be easy to restore balance since these bacteria live naturally in the body already. 
It’s also important to understand that everyone’s gut is unique and no two people will benefit from the exact same balance of bacteria. The process starts before you’re born, and is partially reliant on your mother’s microbiota. As you come into the world and grow, your own diet and lifestyle will greatly affect your gut flora and what balance works for you. 
Probiotics

To sum it up, the difference between prebiotics and probiotics isn’t only one vowel. What is a Long Island Iced Tea?
History of the Long Island Iced Tea
Premade Long Island Iced Tea with Real Tea

structured_data.articleBody:
Patio season is almost upon us, and that means it’s time to get ready for summer cocktails! While cocktails are in fact delicious, there are some to look out for if you’re working on your gut health. For example, let’s talk about the Long Island Iced Tea.You probably already know that this drink does not traditionally contain tea. A Long Island Iced Tea is made with 5 liquors and sugary cola. If you buy premade long island iced tea, there is usually extra sugar added, too.
This boozy concoction is extremely popular. It’s easy to drink despite being mostly alcohol and tastes great. If you ask someone when the last time they had a premade Long Island iced tea was, they likely don’t remember. That’s the point of the drink, right?

When you drink alcohol, it’s terrible for your gut health. It causes bloating and other issues that are never fun the next day. While you won’t be able to rid yourself of the hangover entirely, eliminating options with high sugar can help. 
So, if you’re a fan of getting boozy on the weekends, or whenever, long islands may be your go-to. Let’s go over some facts about the drink, and how you can make an alternative premade long island iced tea that can help with unpleasant alcohol side effects. 
What is a Long Island Iced Tea?
To start, a Long Island Iced Tea is NOT tea. The drink gets its name because when it’s all mixed together it looks like iced tea. This can be deceiving, and dangerous when you’re tempted to chug 8 of them on a night out because they’re so good. A traditional LIIT includes:


 Vodka


 Gin


 Rum


 Tequila


 Triple Sec


 Simple Syrup


 Cola


 Lemon


Don’t be fooled by that color, this drink packs an insane punch. A traditional long island iced tea is going to have an alcohol concentration of around 22%. Somehow, this concoction of several liquors is very easy to drink. Paired with a decent special on price and you’re in for a rough morning the next day.  
In theory, a cup full of 5 different liquors should not taste good. But, with the combination of lemon, cola, and triple sec you get a delicious drink. Triple sec is an orange-flavored liqueur that ties the drink together. 
Another thing to consider before drinking a Long Island Iced Tea is the amount of sugar and calories you’ll be ingesting. An average 8oz Long Island can have around 275 calories and 33 grams of sugar. So, if you’re looking to avoid high sugar drinks, it may be best to stay away from the long island. Premade Long Island Iced Teas can be just as bad if not worse since they are typically made with added sugar and sometimes preservatives. 
History of the Long Island Iced Tea 
So, how did this drink that’s almost all alcohol get its start? There are actually several origin stories and the topic continues to be a debate. Next time you’re sipping a premade Long Island Iced Tea, you can spout off some trivia to your friends.
Long Island, Tennesee
Our first origin story begins in Tennessee. In the community of Long Island inside Kingsport Tennessee, prohibition was not getting in the way for one mixologist. The drink was called the “Old Man Bishop” after its creator, surprisingly named, Old Man Bishop. 
The drink consisted of rum, vodka, whiskey, gin, tequila, and maple syrup. It makes sense that during a time when alcohol was hard to come by that you’d want your drink to pack a huge punch. It’s said that Old Man Bishop’s son, Ransom Bishop refined the drink turning it into the Long Island we know today. This story is not totally confirmed, but it’s a fun piece of trivia. 
Long Island, New York 
When most people think of a Long Island, their first thought is New York, not Tennessee. This story centers around a bartender named Robert “Rosebud” Butt. No matter which story you tell about Long Island Iced Tea, you’re going to find some cool names. 
Butt claims to have invented the drink as a contest entry in 1972. He even had a website stating that he did in fact create the drink but admits there may have been similar cocktails before it. The website doesn’t appear to exist anymore, but an article on Thrillist has his statement:
“The world-famous Long Island Iced Tea was first invented in 1972 by me, Robert Butt, while I was tending bar at the infamous Oak Beach Inn. I participated in a cocktail-creating contest. Triple Sec had to be included, and the bottles started flying. My concoction was an immediate hit and quickly became the house drink at the Oak Beach Inn. By the mid-1970s, every bar on Long Island was serving up this innocent-looking cocktail, and by the 1980s it was known the world over.” 
In an interview with PBS, it’s mentioned that Butt even drove around in a car with the license plate, “LI ICE TEA.” You can watch an interview with Robert “Rosebud” Butt here.
Betty Crocker 
While the two prior stories give verbal credit to inventors of the drink, the first time it was seen printed in a book was in 1961. This was in Betty Crocker’s New Picture Cookbook and there is still a listing on the website for the cocktail recipe today. Butt never acknowledged this, even though it was published before he gives himself the credit. 
A recipe for a Long Island Iced Tea was also published in 1966 in The American All-Purpose Cookbook by Virginia T. Habeeb.  
The next time you’re sipping on cocktails with your friends, bring all of this up. There is much debate on the subject and can be a fun party conversation. 
Premade Long Island Iced Tea 
If you don’t feel like spending the money at the bar every time you want to suck a LIIT down, there are several premade long island iced teas on the market. The problem is these drinks are packed with sugar and can cause a boatload of bloating and other problems in the morning.

One of the most popular premade Long Island Iced Teas is from the Captain Morgan brand. With high sugar content and lots of ingredients, if you are wanting a healthier alternative, you can make your own premade long island iced tea to have on hand for when the urge for happy hour strikes.  
To make a premade Long Island Iced Tea batch with less sugar, we recommend using actual tea. That way, you can remove simple syrup and cola. It may taste different, but you might like it better! 
Premade Long Island Iced Tea with Real Tea 
First, you’ll need your ingredients. For the tea, we suggest Half Day’s Lemon Black Tea. You’ll get the sweet flavor with less sugar, and with added fiber and prebiotics. Not that this will totally eliminate the hangover in the morning but your gut will thank you.

Ingredients 


 1//2 cup tequila 


 ½ cup white rum 


 ½ cup gin


 ½ cup triple sec


 ¾ cup lemon juice 


 1 ½ cups iced tea of your choice


 Lemons for garnish 


Step 1
Mix all ingredients except the tea in a bowl until chilled 
Step 2
Strain the boozy mixture into a pitcher, then add the tea 
Step 3
Pour over ice, serve, and enjoy! Cut up lemon wedges to use as garnish 
Making a pitcher of premade Long Island Iced Tea will save you time. It’s an easy party drink that’s a total crowd-pleaser, too. Replacing the cola will remove the carbonation, and if you feel you’re missing that you can add soda water for some bubbles. Keep in mind that carbonation can irritate your gut even when it’s not in a sugary soda. 
Conclusion
To sum it up, premade Long Island Iced teas can be a lifesaver at parties. It’s best to avoid store-bought options that are full of sugar and other things. The history of Long Island is also an interesting party topic, so you can bust out your newfound trivia as you serve guests delicious drinks.

pages.main_text: Premade Long Island Iced Tea With Less Bloating March 28, 2022 Share Share Link Close share Copy link Patio season is almost upon us, and that means it’s time to get ready for summer cocktails! While cocktails are in fact delicious, there are some to look out for if you’re working on your gut health. For example, let’s talk about the Long Island Iced Tea. You probably already know that this drink does not traditionally contain tea. A Long Island Iced Tea is made with 5 liquors and sugary cola. If you buy premade long island iced tea, there is usually extra sugar added, too. This boozy concoction is extremely popular. It’s easy to drink despite being mostly alcohol and tastes great. If you ask someone when the last time they had a premade Long Island iced tea was, they likely don’t remember. That’s the point of the drink, right? When you drink alcohol, it’s terrible for your gut health. It causes bloating and other issues that are never fun the next day. While you won’t be able to rid yourself of the hangover entirely, eliminating options with high sugar can help. So, if you’re a fan of getting boozy on the weekends, or whenever, long islands may be your go-to. Let’s go over some facts about the drink, and how you can make an alternative premade long island iced tea that can help with unpleasant alcohol side effects. What is a Long Island Iced Tea? To start, a Long Island Iced Tea is NOT tea. The drink gets its name because when it’s all mixed together it looks like iced tea. This can be deceiving, and dangerous when you’re tempted to chug 8 of them on a night out because they’re so good. A traditional LIIT includes: Vodka Gin Rum Tequila Triple Sec Simple Syrup Cola Lemon Don’t be fooled by that color, this drink packs an insane punch. A traditional long island iced tea is going to have an alcohol concentration of around 22%. Somehow, this concoction of several liquors is very easy to drink. Paired with a decent special on price and you’re in for a rough morning the next day. In theory, a cup full of 5 different liquors should not taste good. But, with the combination of lemon, cola, and triple sec you get a delicious drink. Triple sec is an orange-flavored liqueur that ties the drink together. Another thing to consider before drinking a Long Island Iced Tea is the amount of sugar and calories you’ll be ingesting. An average 8oz Long Island can have around 275 calories and 33 grams of sugar. So, if you’re looking to avoid high sugar drinks, it may be best to stay away from the long island. Premade Long Island Iced Teas can be just as bad if not worse since they are typically made with added sugar and sometimes preservatives. History of the Long Island Iced Tea So, how did this drink that’s almost all alcohol get its start? There are actually several origin stories and the topic continues to be a debate. Next time you’re sipping a premade Long Island Iced Tea, you can spout off some trivia to your friends. Long Island, Tennesee Our first origin story begins in Tennessee. In the community of Long Island inside Kingsport Tennessee, prohibition was not getting in the way for one mixologist. The drink was called the “Old Man Bishop” after its creator, surprisingly named, Old Man Bishop. The drink consisted of rum, vodka, whiskey, gin, tequila, and maple syrup. It makes sense that during a time when alcohol was hard to come by that you’d want your drink to pack a huge punch. It’s said that Old Man Bishop’s son, Ransom Bishop refined the drink turning it into the Long Island we know today. This story is not totally confirmed, but it’s a fun piece of trivia. Long Island, New York When most people think of a Long Island, their first thought is New York, not Tennessee. This story centers around a bartender named Robert “Rosebud” Butt. No matter which story you tell about Long Island Iced Tea, you’re going to find some cool names. Butt claims to have invented the drink as a contest entry in 1972. He even had a website stating that he did in fact create the drink but admits there may have been similar cocktails before it. The website doesn’t appear to exist anymore, but an article on Thrillist has his statement: “The world-famous Long Island Iced Tea was first invented in 1972 by me, Robert Butt, while I was tending bar at the infamous Oak Beach Inn. I participated in a cocktail-creating contest. Triple Sec had to be included, and the bottles started flying. My concoction was an immediate hit and quickly became the house drink at the Oak Beach Inn. By the mid-1970s, every bar on Long Island was serving up this innocent-looking cocktail, and by the 1980s it was known the world over.” In an interview with PBS, it’s mentioned that Butt even drove around in a car with the license plate, “LI ICE TEA.” You can watch an interview with Robert “Rosebud” Butt here . Betty Crocker While the two prior stories give verbal credit to inventors of the drink, the first time it was seen printed in a book was in 1961. This was in Betty Crocker’s New Picture Cookbook and there is still a listing on the website for the cocktail recipe today. Butt never acknowledged this, even though it was published before he gives himself the credit. A recipe for a Long Island Iced Tea was also published in 1966 in The American All-Purpose Cookbook by Virginia T. Habeeb. The next time you’re sipping on cocktails with your friends, bring all of this up. There is much debate on the subject and can be a fun party conversation. Premade Long Island Iced Tea If you don’t feel like spending the money at the bar every time you want to suck a LIIT down, there are several premade long island iced teas on the market. The problem is these drinks are packed with sugar and can cause a boatload of bloating and other problems in the morning. One of the most popular premade Long Island Iced Teas is from the Captain Morgan brand. With high sugar content and lots of ingredients, if you are wanting a healthier alternative, you can make your own premade long island iced tea to have on hand for when the urge for happy hour strikes. To make a premade Long Island Iced Tea batch with less sugar, we recommend using actual tea. That way, you can remove simple syrup and cola. It may taste different, but you might like it better! Premade Long Island Iced Tea with Real Tea First, you’ll need your ingredients. For the tea, we suggest Half Day’s Lemon Black Tea . You’ll get the sweet flavor with less sugar, and with added fiber and prebiotics. Not that this will totally eliminate the hangover in the morning but your gut will thank you. Ingredients 1//2 cup tequila ½ cup white rum ½ cup gin ½ cup triple sec ¾ cup lemon juice 1 ½ cups iced tea of your choice Lemons for garnish Step 1 Mix all ingredients except the tea in a bowl until chilled Step 2 Strain the boozy mixture into a pitcher, then add the tea Step 3 Pour over ice, serve, and enjoy! Cut up lemon wedges to use as garnish Making a pitcher of premade Long Island Iced Tea will save you time. It’s an easy party drink that’s a total crowd-pleaser, too. Replacing the cola will remove the carbonation, and if you feel you’re missing that you can add soda water for some bubbles. Keep in mind that carbonation can irritate your gut even when it’s not in a sugary soda. Conclusion To sum it up, premade Long Island Iced teas can be a lifesaver at parties. It’s best to avoid store-bought options that are full of sugar and other things. The history of Long Island is also an interesting party topic, so you can bust out your newfound trivia as you serve guests delicious drinks. Try replacing the cola and simple syrup with real tea to lower the amount of sugar you’re consuming. With a Long Island, you’re already getting a lot of calories from the 5 liquors in there. Any little bit helps when it comes to taking care of your gut! Back to blog

structured_data.articleBody:
If you're like most people, you've probably experienced the discomfort and embarrassment of bloating at some point in your life. It's a common problem that can be caused by many things, such as eating too much, drinking too much alcohol, stress, or even taking certain medications. 
Fortunately, there is a simple solution: probiotics! Probiotics are beneficial bacteria that help keep your gut healthy and functioning properly. In this blog post, we will discuss everything you need to know about bloating, as well as the best teas and probiotics for bloating, such as Halfday's tea tonics, to get relief from your symptoms!

 
What Causes Bloating?
There are many different things that can cause bloating, but the most common culprit is a buildup of gas in the intestines. This can be caused by eating foods that are high in carbohydrates, such as bread or pasta, or drinking carbonated beverages. Eating too much food at once can also lead to bloating, as your stomach has to work overtime to digest all of the food. 
Certain medical conditions, such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), can also cause bloating. IBS is a chronic condition that affects the large intestine and can cause symptoms like abdominal pain, cramping, diarrhea, and constipation. If you think you may have IBS, it's essential to talk to your doctor so they can properly diagnose and treat the condition.
Stress is another common cause of bloating, as it can lead to changes in gut bacteria and motility (the movement of food through the digestive system). In addition, when you're stressed, your body produces the hormone cortisol, which can have a negative impact on gut health. As you can see, there are a ton of different reasons why you might feel bloated. 
How Do Probiotics Help With Bloating?
Probiotics are live microorganisms (usually bacteria) that are similar to the ones already present in our gut. They can be taken in the form of supplements, foods, or probiotic-rich beverages like kombucha or kefir. Probiotics help maintain a healthy balance of gut bacteria and have been shown to provide numerous health benefits, including relief from bloating. 
When probiotics are taken in supplement form, they can help to replenish the good bacteria in your gut that may have been lost due to a change in diet or antibiotic use. Probiotic supplements can also help break down gas-producing carbohydrates, which can reduce the amount of gas that builds up in the intestines and cause bloating. 
There are many different probiotic supplements on the market, so it's essential to choose one that is high quality and contains various strains of probiotics. Half-day tea tonics are a great alternative as they are made with all-natural ingredients and don't have the bitter taste of regular probiotics.

 
What Are The Best Ways To Relieve Bloating?
In addition to probiotics, you can do a few other things to relieve bloating. This includes: 
Avoiding Trigger Foods
First, try to avoid trigger foods that make your symptoms worse. Common triggers include dairy, wheat, soy, caffeine, and sugar. Eating smaller meals more often can also help, as it will give your stomach a chance to digest the food properly. If you notice that one particular food seems to trigger your bloating, it's best to avoid it altogether. 
Drinking Plenty of Water
Second, make sure you're drinking plenty of water. Dehydration can make bloating worse, so staying hydrated throughout the day is essential. Drinking herbal tea or warm water with lemon can also help to relieve bloating. 
Exercising
Regular exercise can help to improve gut motility and reduce bloating. A moderate amount of exercise is the best way to go, as too much high-intensity exercise can worsen your symptoms. Walking, yoga, and Pilates are all great exercises to try if you're looking to reduce bloating. 
Don't Overeat
If you tend to overeat, it's important to make a conscious effort to stop. Eating smaller meals more often can help, as well as avoiding trigger foods. Chewing your food slowly and properly can also help, as it allows your stomach time to properly digest the food. 
Try A Low-FODMAP Diet
If you have IBS, you may want to try a low-FODMAP diet. This diet eliminates high-FODMAP foods, which are known to trigger IBS symptoms. Foods that are high in FODMAPs include dairy, wheat, soy, and certain fruits and vegetables. By eliminating these foods from your diet, you may be able to reduce your bloating. 
Reduce Your Stress
Did you know that stress can actually make your bloating worse? This is because stress can lead to changes in gut bacteria and motility. If you're looking to reduce your bloating, it's crucial to find ways to reduce your stress. This may include exercise, meditation, or deep breathing exercises. 
Reduce Your Sugar Intake
Sugar can feed the harmful bacteria in your gut and cause bloating. If you're looking to reduce your bloating, it's crucial to reduce your sugar intake. This means avoiding sugary foods and drinks, as well as processed foods that contain hidden sugars.

Get Plenty Of Sleep
Did you know that lack of sleep can also make your bloating worse? This is because when you're tired, your body produces more cortisol, leading to changes in gut bacteria. If you're looking to reduce your bloating, it's important to get plenty of rest. Aim for at least eight hours of sleep per night. 
How to Choose the Best Probiotic for Bloating
When it comes to probiotics, there are many different products on the market, so how do you know which one is right for you? The first step is to identify your goals for taking probiotics. Are you looking to improve gut health, reduce bloating, or both? Once you know what you want to achieve, you can narrow down your probiotic options. 
When choosing a probiotic supplement, it's essential to look for one that contains multiple strains of probiotics. This is because different strains can offer different health benefits. For example, the strain Lactobacillus acidophilus is known for its ability to reduce bloating, while Bifidobacterium bifidum has been shown to improve gut health.
Lastly, you'll want to choose a probiotic that's fun to drink! If you can't stand the taste of probiotics, you're not likely to stick with them. So look for a probiotic that's flavored or comes in a convenient powder form that can be added to smoothies or juices. 
Top Probiotics For Bloating
Now that you know how to choose the best probiotics for bloating, let's look at some of the best options on the market.

Garden of Life Dr. Formulated Probiotics: This probiotic supplement contains 16 different strains of probiotics, as well as prebiotics and probiotic-created vitamins, minerals, and enzymes.

Jarrow Formulas Jarrow-Dophilus EPS: This probiotic supplement contains eight strains of probiotics that are designed to survive stomach acid. It's also non-GMO and dairy-free.

Renew Life Ultimate Flora Extra Care Probiotic: This probiotic supplement contains 50 billion live cultures from 12 different strains of probiotics. It's also dairy-free, gluten-free, and vegetarian.

Fortunately, there is a simple solution: probiotics! Probiotics are beneficial bacteria that help keep your gut healthy and functioning properly. In this blog post, we will discuss everything you need to know about bloating, as well as the best teas and probiotics for bloating, such as Halfday's tea tonics , to get relief from your symptoms! What Causes Bloating? There are many different things that can cause bloating, but the most common culprit is a buildup of gas in the intestines. This can be caused by eating foods that are high in carbohydrates, such as bread or pasta, or drinking carbonated beverages. Eating too much food at once can also lead to bloating, as your stomach has to work overtime to digest all of the food. Certain medical conditions, such as irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), can also cause bloating. IBS is a chronic condition that affects the large intestine and can cause symptoms like abdominal pain, cramping, diarrhea, and constipation. If you think you may have IBS, it's essential to talk to your doctor so they can properly diagnose and treat the condition. Stress is another common cause of bloating, as it can lead to changes in gut bacteria and motility (the movement of food through the digestive system). In addition, when you're stressed, your body produces the hormone cortisol, which can have a negative impact on gut health. As you can see, there are a ton of different reasons why you might feel bloated. How Do Probiotics Help With Bloating? Probiotics are live microorganisms (usually bacteria) that are similar to the ones already present in our gut. They can be taken in the form of supplements, foods, or probiotic-rich beverages like kombucha or kefir. Probiotics help maintain a healthy balance of gut bacteria and have been shown to provide numerous health benefits, including relief from bloating. When probiotics are taken in supplement form, they can help to replenish the good bacteria in your gut that may have been lost due to a change in diet or antibiotic use. Probiotic supplements can also help break down gas-producing carbohydrates, which can reduce the amount of gas that builds up in the intestines and cause bloating. There are many different probiotic supplements on the market, so it's essential to choose one that is high quality and contains various strains of probiotics. Half-day tea tonics are a great alternative as they are made with all-natural ingredients and don't have the bitter taste of regular probiotics. What Are The Best Ways To Relieve Bloating? In addition to probiotics, you can do a few other things to relieve bloating. This includes: Avoiding Trigger Foods First, try to avoid trigger foods that make your symptoms worse. Common triggers include dairy, wheat, soy, caffeine, and sugar. Eating smaller meals more often can also help, as it will give your stomach a chance to digest the food properly. If you notice that one particular food seems to trigger your bloating, it's best to avoid it altogether. Drinking Plenty of Water Second, make sure you're drinking plenty of water. Dehydration can make bloating worse, so staying hydrated throughout the day is essential. Drinking herbal tea or warm water with lemon can also help to relieve bloating. Exercising Regular exercise can help to improve gut motility and reduce bloating. A moderate amount of exercise is the best way to go, as too much high-intensity exercise can worsen your symptoms. Walking, yoga, and Pilates are all great exercises to try if you're looking to reduce bloating. Don't Overeat If you tend to overeat, it's important to make a conscious effort to stop. Eating smaller meals more often can help, as well as avoiding trigger foods. Chewing your food slowly and properly can also help, as it allows your stomach time to properly digest the food. Try A Low-FODMAP Diet If you have IBS, you may want to try a low-FODMAP diet. This diet eliminates high-FODMAP foods, which are known to trigger IBS symptoms. Foods that are high in FODMAPs include dairy, wheat, soy, and certain fruits and vegetables. By eliminating these foods from your diet, you may be able to reduce your bloating. Reduce Your Stress Did you know that stress can actually make your bloating worse ? This is because stress can lead to changes in gut bacteria and motility. If you're looking to reduce your bloating, it's crucial to find ways to reduce your stress. This may include exercise, meditation, or deep breathing exercises. Reduce Your Sugar Intake Sugar can feed the harmful bacteria in your gut and cause bloating. If you're looking to reduce your bloating, it's crucial to reduce your sugar intake. This means avoiding sugary foods and drinks, as well as processed foods that contain hidden sugars. Get Plenty Of Sleep Did you know that lack of sleep can also make your bloating worse? This is because when you're tired, your body produces more cortisol, leading to changes in gut bacteria. If you're looking to reduce your bloating, it's important to get plenty of rest. Aim for at least eight hours of sleep per night. How to Choose the Best Probiotic for Bloating When it comes to probiotics, there are many different products on the market, so how do you know which one is right for you? The first step is to identify your goals for taking probiotics. Are you looking to improve gut health, reduce bloating, or both? Once you know what you want to achieve, you can narrow down your probiotic options. When choosing a probiotic supplement, it's essential to look for one that contains multiple strains of probiotics. This is because different strains can offer different health benefits. For example, the strain Lactobacillus acidophilus is known for its ability to reduce bloating, while Bifidobacterium bifidum has been shown to improve gut health. Lastly, you'll want to choose a probiotic that's fun to drink! If you can't stand the taste of probiotics, you're not likely to stick with them. So look for a probiotic that's flavored or comes in a convenient powder form that can be added to smoothies or juices. Jarrow Formulas Jarrow-Dophilus EPS: This probiotic supplement contains eight strains of probiotics that are designed to survive stomach acid. It's also non-GMO and dairy-free. Renew Life Ultimate Flora Extra Care Probiotic : This probiotic supplement contains 50 billion live cultures from 12 different strains of probiotics. structured_data.articleBody:
Do you often feel bloated after eating? If so, you're not alone. Unfortunately, bloating is a common problem that more than 25% of people experience on a regular basis. Fortunately, there are drinks that can help reduce bloating and make you feel more comfortable. In this blog post, we will discuss 11 drinks that can help with bloating as well as what causes bloating in the first place. 

What Is Bloating, And Why Does It Occur?
Bloating is a condition that results in the stomach feeling full and tight. It can cause discomfort and pain in the abdominal area. Many different factors can contribute to bloating, such as:

Eating large meals
Eating fatty or greasy foods
Eating gas-producing foods (such as beans, cabbage, and broccoli)
Eating too quickly
Drinking carbonated beverages
Constipation
PMS
Menstruation
Anxiety or stress
Certain medical conditions (such as irritable bowel syndrome, celiac disease, and Crohn's disease)

Fortunately, you don't have to suffer through bloating. There are plenty of beverage options you can choose from to help you feel better. 
Foods That Contribute To Bloating
Before we get into the drinks that help with bloating, let's first discuss some of the foods that can contribute to it. As we mentioned earlier, gas-producing foods are a common cause of bloating. This is because they contain high levels of fiber which the body cannot break down. When these fibers reach the large intestine, they are fermented by bacteria, producing gas. 
Other foods that can contribute to bloating include those high in sodium (such as processed foods, canned soups, and salad dressings) and those containing lactose (dairy products). Some of the top foods you should avoid if you want to help yourself get rid of bloating include: 
Beans
Beans are a healthy food that is high in fiber and protein. However, they can also cause bloating for some people. This is because they contain oligosaccharides, which are a type of carbohydrate that the body cannot break down. 
Lentils
While lentils are a great source of fiber, they can also cause bloating for some people. So it's best to avoid lentils if you're trying to reduce this issue in your body. 
Brocolli
Brocolli is a healthy vegetable that is high in fiber. However, it can also cause bloating for some people. If you suffer from bloating after eating broccoli, you may want to try steaming it instead of eating it raw. 
Cabbage
Cabbage is a healthy vegetable that is high in fiber. However, it can also cause bloating for some people. If you suffer from bloating after eating cabbage, you may want to try fermentation instead of eating it raw.  
Top 11 Drinks That Help With Bloating
Figuring out what drinks help with bloating can be tricky. That's because different drinks work for different people. Some drinks that might help reduce bloating for one person may not have the same effect on another person. With that said, here are 11 drinks that help with bloating: 

1. Half-day's Green Tea With Honey Ginseng:

Ginger is a popular natural remedy for many different stomach issues, including bloating. This is because it can help to reduce inflammation and gas in the digestive system. Half-day's Green Tea With Honey Ginseng is an excellent option if you're looking for something to help with bloating. The honey and ginseng work together to help relieve abdominal pain and discomfort while providing a ton of antioxidants to reduce inflammation in your body. Plus, with the extra fiber, you'll find a boost in your overall gut health, making it a great choice for when you're feeling bloated. 




2. Lemon Water

Lemon water is a simple, yet effective, drink for bloating relief. The citrus fruit helps to stimulate the digestive system and promote regularity. Lemon water can also help to reduce inflammation in the gut. For best results, drink a glass of lemon water first thing in the morning on an empty stomach. If you're looking for something a little tastier, we recommend trying the lemon black iced tea from Drink Half Day. Not only does it provide the same impact as drinking lemon water, but it's also refreshing and delicious. 


3. Berry Smoothie

A berry smoothie is a great option if you're looking for something that's both delicious and nutritious. Berries are high in fiber, which can help with bloating by promoting regularity. They're also a good source of antioxidants, which can help to reduce inflammation in the body. For a tasty and refreshing berry smoothie, try combining strawberries, blueberries, and blackberries with water to enjoy the extra vitamins and minerals as well as a decrease in bloating. 

4. Chamomile Tea

Chamomile tea is a popular herbal tea that has many health benefits. It's known to be soothing and relaxing, which can help with bloating caused by stress or anxiety. Chamomile tea can also help to reduce inflammation in the gut. For best results, drink chamomile tea before bedtime to help relieve bloating overnight, as it may cause you to feel sleepy.

5. Ginger Tea

As we mentioned before, ginger is an excellent natural remedy for bloating. It can help to reduce inflammation and gas in the digestive system. Ginger tea is a great way to get your daily dose of ginger while also reaping the benefits of drinking warm tea. For best results, drink ginger tea after meals to help with digestion.

6. Kombucha Drinks

Kombucha drinks are a great option if you're looking for a probiotic-rich beverage. Probiotics are live bacteria that can help improve gut health. They can also help reduce bloating by balancing the good and bad bacteria in your gut. Kombucha drinks are typically made with green or black tea, so you'll also get the added benefits of those drinks as well. 

7. Water with Mint Leaves

Mint is a popular herb that's known for its calming and soothing effects. It can also help reduce bloating by relieving gas and cramps in the stomach. For best results, add a few mint leaves to your water bottle or glass of water and let them steep for a few minutes before drinking.

8. Coconut Water

Coconut water is an excellent option if you're looking for something that's hydrating and refreshing. It's also a good source of electrolytes, which can help to reduce bloating caused by dehydration. Coconut water is also rich in potassium, which can help relieve cramps and bloating. You can either choose to drink it plain or add it to a smoothie for an extra boost of hydration. For example, pairing it with a berry smoothie would be a great way to get the benefits of both drinks. 

9. Watermelon Juice

Watermelon juice is a refreshing and hydrating drink that's perfect for summer. It's also a good source of lycopene, an antioxidant that can help to reduce inflammation in the body. Watermelon juice is also rich in electrolytes, which can help to prevent dehydration and bloating. For best results, drink watermelon juice on its own or add it to a smoothie or cocktail.

10. Green Juice

Green juice is an excellent option if you're looking for a nutrient-rich drink. It's made with leafy greens, which are a good source of vitamins and minerals. Greens are also rich in chlorophyll, which can help to reduce bloating by cleansing the digestive system. Some greens to add to your juice may include spinach, kale, and Swiss chard. For best results, drink green juice on an empty stomach or before meals. 

11. Pineapple Juice

Last, but not least, pineapple juice is a great option for reducing bloating. It contains bromelain, an enzyme that helps to break down proteins and reduce inflammation. Pineapple juice is also rich in fiber and water, which can help to promote regularity and prevent dehydration. For best results, drink pineapple juice on its own or add it to a smoothie or cocktail. 
Conclusion
There are many drinks that help with bloating. Some of the best options include chamomile tea, ginger tea, kombucha drinks, water with mint leaves, coconut water, watermelon juice, green juice, and pineapple juice. Experiment with different drinks to see what works best for you. And be sure to stay hydrated and drink plenty of fluids throughout the day to help reduce bloating. Thanks for reading!

pages.description: Trying to understand more about ulcerative colitis and how it may impact you? Let's dig in to learn more about causes, symptoms, and how it can be avoided.

structured_data.articleBody:
Gut health can keep you from feeling 100% and can be impacted by tons of small yet important factors in your life like your diet, hydration, and vitamin intake. Gut health refers to the entire gastrointestinal tract including the intestines, stomach, and colon. Typically, when one area of the gut is irritated or inflamed, it affects the rest of the system. Bacteria play an important role in the gut and allow you to digest food and beverages properly. If you’re not careful with your gut health, it can be more than the discomfort that’s an issue.  
Heartburn, bloating, nausea and fatigue are some of the common ones. If poor gut health goes untreated, it can also trigger more serious issues. Ulcerative Colitis is an example. It can range from mild symptoms to life-threatening, so we take it pretty seriously. While doctors aren’t totally sure what directly leads to it, studies have shown bad gut health can lead to symptoms and flare-ups.  
Before running off to Reddit, Health MD, or other online sources to diagnose yourself with Ulcerative Colitis, it’s important to know the facts and home remedies that can help you maintain a healthy gut and avoid triggers. Let’s talk about gut health, UC, and dietary solutions to keep symptoms away. 
What is Ulcerative Colitis?
To start, we already know UC is a form of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD.) These diseases can be confusing to navigate because the symptoms are similar. The term ulcerative indicates that the disease causes ulcers within the colon that can be painful and harmful to your health. All forms of IBD can cause bloating and gas, which will make you want to throw away every pair of tight pants you own. 
UC primarily affects the entirety of the digestive tract. This includes the inner lining of the large intestine otherwise known as the colon, small intestine, and rectum. We know, not a fun area to talk about but it’s important to understand what can go wrong if your gut health is imbalanced.  
   The most common symptoms of Ulcerative Colitis are:


 Diarrhea 


 Rectal pain


 Weight loss 


 Rectal bleeding 


 Fatigue 


 Fever 


 These symptoms are common in most forms of IBD, so if you’re experiencing them it’s important to see a doctor. Browsing the ulcerative colitis Reddit page can be a place to compare your symptoms with others, but you will need a formal diagnosis for treatment. 
Currently, there is no known cure for UC. While that sounds terrifying, most cases of  ulcerative colitis will be mild and can be treated at home once you know the problem. Typically, those with UC will experience occasional flare-ups due to eating or drinking certain things. There are several types of UC that affect different areas of the digestive tract.
Ulcerative Proctitis
This type of UC happens closest to the rectum, and the telltale sign is rectal bleeding. Typical symptoms include bloating, abdominal pain, and constipation. Bloating and gas can also be symptoms associated with this type of UC. 
Proctosigmoiditis
Proctosigmoiditis is a form of UC that affects the rectum as well as the sigmoid colon. The sigmoid colon is a connection between the intestine and the rectum, making it a crucial part of the digestive tract. Symptoms include abdominal pain, weight loss, and fever. 
Left-Sided Colitis
The name says it all for this one. Left-sided colitis occurs in the left side of your digestive tract. Symptoms include bloody diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and pain on the left side with an urgency to have a bowel movement. 
Pancolitis
This one affects the colon and will cause bloody diarrhea, significant weight loss, fatigue, and abdominal cramping. You’ll also experience a significant amount of bloating. 
No form of UC is going to be fun to deal with, but knowing what kind you have will be helpful with treating your symptoms and finding relief from bloating and gas. In some cases, surgery may be necessary to resolve the issue. Surgery includes removing the colon and rerouting it into a stoma in the abdomen. Excrement will be collected in a pouch attached to the body. If you’re on TikTok, there are a few influencers who explain what it’s like to live with a stoma. 
Once you know your diagnosis, you can join the ulcerative colitis Reddit to connect with others! 
What Causes Ulcerative Colitis?
There is no specific known cause of ulcerative colitis, but there are several suggestions. Some experts say it’s hereditary, and others say it could be an autoimmune problem. Diet and stress were thought to be potential causes, but now they are considered triggers of the condition when it’s already present.  
Flare-ups can be caused by eating spicy food, drinking carbonated beverages, or even stress. It’s important to maintain a healthy lifestyle if you’re living with UC. When you aren’t dealing with a flare-up, you can be more flexible with your diet, but always be aware that triggers can cause one. 
When UC is flaring up, the immune system triggers a response to get rid of the bad bacteria in the gut. This is why it could potentially be caused by an autoimmune dysfunction in the body. It’s important to also look at your family medical history. If your relatives have dealt with UC, it’s possible that you will too. 
While there isn’t an exact cause of UC, a study at Stanford states that people who suffer from UC could be missing an essential gut microbe. The microbe that is missing helps to create secondary bile acids that are vital to your gut health. If you have UC, it’s crucial to improve your gut health to maintain function and avoid discomfort from the dreaded gas and bloating. 
The majority of people who experience UC in their life will start showing symptoms before they turn 30. Again, symptoms may be mild and happen so little that you may not know you have UC for a while. If you’re experiencing frequent bouts of gas and bloating, it’s important to seek out a medical opinion to see if it could be due to an underlying disease like ulcerative colitis. 
Treatment for Ulcerative Colitis
Surgery is typically a last resort for people diagnosed with UC. Typically, medications and home remedies will do the trick. 
Medications 
Medications aren’t going to cure UC, but accompanied diet and exercise can help you maintain your gut health. The medications will work to reduce inflammation and can keep symptoms at bay during a flare-up. 
Diet and Nutrition
One of the best things you can do for yourself is paying close attention to your diet for ulcerative colitis. Even when you’re not dealing with a flare-up, a consistent diet free of triggers will keep you happy and free of bloating. Ulcerative colitis can reduce your appetite which causes weight loss and an inability to absorb nutrients. This is why a healthy diet is so important.  
Food and Drink to Avoid:


 Carbonated drinks


 Caffeine


 Alcohol


 Spicy Food


Dietary Suggestions:


 Soft, bland food


 Pasta


 White Rice 


 Oatmeal


 Potatoes 


 Lean Proteins such as eggs, chicken, and tofu


 Foods with omega 3 fatty acids such as fish


 Non-carbonated drinks

Probiotics / Prebiotics

People on ulcerative colitis Reddit discuss that everyone’s triggers may be different, and you’ll need to get to know what’s right for you. Paleo, gluten-free, and low-fiber diets tend to be good starting points. 
One thing you can do to improve your diet for gut health is to use prebiotics. Prebiotics will help feed the good bacteria in your gut and give it the energy to fend off the build-up of bad bacteria. Having a consistent diet full of prebiotics will keep your gut happy and free of bloating. 
Incorporating foods with prebiotics in them is an easy way to have a gut-healthy diet. Eating foods like bananas, onions, garlic and soybeans will help you increase your prebiotic intake without thinking about it. You should also avoid things like coffee and fizzy drinks that can trigger a flare-up pretty quickly.

If you are struggling with giving up carbonated drinks and coffee, try Halfday. Halfday is a prebiotic packed iced-tea. It’s a great alternative for people with UC because it’s non-carbonated and packed with prebiotics to keep your gut in good shape. Other probiotic / prebiotic alternatives like kombucha have carbonation, so can trigger bloating. There’s a variety of flavors to choose from, so you don’t have to say goodbye to flavor to care for your gut. 
Ulcerative Colitis and Gut Health 
The intestines are a wild place. They’re home to trillions of microorganisms that affect your gut. Good and bad bacteria reside in the gut and can disagree with each other to cause problems. People living with UC generally don’t have the normal levels of bacteria in their gut, which can cause other problems such as gas and bloat. 
Conclusion
The bottom line is that ulcerative colitis isn’t the end of the world. The symptoms are unpleasant and can lead to discomfort and bloating. With no known cure, all you can do is practice self-care and listen to your gut, literally. If it’s making noises, it may be time to see a doctor. Stay away from spicy food and fizzy drinks to keep your colon happy.

headings.text: Schedule Workouts and Stick to Them
Eat Red and Purple Fruits and Vegetables

structured_data.articleBody:
Weight loss can be tricky, there’s no doubt about it. If you’ve been trying to lose weight, you’ve surely gone online to find tips. It’s important to remember that everyone is different, and the most popular tips might not work for you and your body. Don’t get discouraged! There are tons of underrated weight loss tips out there to try and find what works for you.  

It can get overwhelming trying to sift through the internet and find the weight loss tips that will work for your lifestyle. Sometimes it’s necessary to go off the beaten path and try the underrated tips. Not everyone is trying to lose weight for the same reasons either. You might want to shed a few pounds for the summer, improve your mental health, or work on your gut. Whatever the reason may be, there are underrated weight loss tips to help! 
Keep a Journal 
Since keeping a journal doesn’t directly help you with weight loss, it’s an underrated tip. There are, however, several studies that show it’s an effective method for holding yourself accountable on your weight loss journey. You can also use your journal to keep track of your eating schedule and track when you get hungry.  
Not only that, but if you’re working on a diet to improve your mood, you can track your thoughts and feelings so you can see if you’re making any progress. If you’ve been having anxiety about weight loss and getting started, putting pen to paper is a great way to get everything out of your mind. Your journal is a safe space to chronicle your thoughts. 
Schedule Workouts and Stick to Them 
Working out is typically one of the main components of most weight loss journeys. Exercise is proven to increase metabolism and help you burn those unwanted calories. It’s also fabulous for your mental health. While working out itself isn’t an underrated weight loss tip, making a workout schedule is. 
It can be super hard to get into a good routine when it comes to working out, so setting specific times and days can help you stay on track. Sure, signing up for the gym is great but going sporadically may not bring you the results you’re looking for.  
Having scheduled dates and classes can also help you be mentally and physically prepared for your workout. A good motivator is to sign up for a place that you have to pay for. If you don’t go, you’re losing money! Another good tip is to enlist a workout buddy to hold you accountable to show up for your classes or workout times. You can also use your journal to keep track!  
Be Realistic 
Don’t be fooled by Instagram influencers. You're not going to achieve your goals overnight by cutting out sugar and drinking whatever product they’re selling. If you like to eat bread and it isn’t causing you problems like bloating and gas, keep eating it! 
Bread and pasta contain carbs that are going to give you energy throughout the day and for your scheduled workouts. Don’t set goals for yourself that you won’t be able to obtain, remember that slow and steady wins the race. Patience is key when it comes to weight loss. 
Keep it Chilly 
Temperature probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind when you’re thinking about weight loss. Another underrated weight loss tip is to turn the thermostat down at night. The cooler temperature can trigger your body to convert fat that’s been sitting there into usable fat that burns up to keep your body warm. Now, that doesn’t mean you should be sleeping in an icebox every night, but keeping it cool and sleeping with more blankets can help. 
Let Yourself Sleep 
One of the best-underrated weight loss tips out there is to sleep more. If you’re sleep-deprived, you’re not going to get the results you’re looking for. You need sleep to increase your metabolism. The recommended amount of sleep is 7 hours or more. 
According to the National Sleep Foundation, lack of sleep can affect your appetite, as well. Your appetite is controlled by neurotransmitters, and sleep regulates them. If you’ve ever been really tired during the day from poor sleep, you’ve probably noticed you want to eat more during the day. This is to compensate for the lack of energy you have from not sleeping enough. You’ll eat more and won’t burn off as many calories. So, let yourself get some rest! 
Replace Snacks With Water 
No, we’re not talking about fasting, but if you’re trying to lose weight you might want to cut back on the snacks. Often when you’re hungry, you’re really just thirsty. So, try drinking a glass of water first and see if you’re hungry afterward. 
Eat Red and Purple Fruits and Vegetables
Alright, stay with us on this one. We’re talking about underrated weight loss tips, right? When you’re picking your fruits and vegetables for the week, look at the colors. Foods that are red and purple have anthocyanins which are antioxidant compounds. These antioxidants not only give foods the red and purple colors, but they can help with inflammation and are known to suppress fat-storing genes. Foods you can eat are: 


 Apples


 Eggplant


 Red Cabbage 


 Blueberries


 Strawberries 


 Prunes


 Grapefruit 

Avoid Stress 
We know this one is difficult. If you’re stressed, you can’t flip a switch and make it go away. When you’re stressed, your body produces cortisol, which is known as the stress hormone. If you’re producing a lot of cortisol, you likely won’t sleep well and your metabolism will take a hit.  
When your cortisol levels are high, your insulin levels tend to increase too. That means you’ll start craving sugary junk that you’re trying to stay away from. If you’re feeling stressed, it’s important to take care of yourself. Try meditation, yoga, or just taking time for yourself away from the stressors of life. 
Drink More Tea 
If you enjoy tea, you’ve probably already read up on the health benefits that come with the territory. Adding tea to your diet is another underrated weight loss tip. Now, we don’t mean grabbing a sugary concoction from the gas station that’s labeled as tea. That’s not going to help. What we do mean is choosing healthy teas that will give you health benefits along with promoting weight loss. 
One of the best teas to drink for weight loss is green tea. There have been several studies on the matter which directly link green tea to weight loss. You can also use your journal to keep track of your eating schedule and track when you get hungry. Not only that, but if you’re working on a diet to improve your mood, you can track your thoughts and feelings so you can see if you’re making any progress. If you’ve been having anxiety about weight loss and getting started, putting pen to paper is a great way to get everything out of your mind. Your journal is a safe space to chronicle your thoughts.
